queryResults.sqlPreview: /*Changes made by Syeravadekar- 09-15-2021 Adding filter for contact_type, fix for missing state values and missing stu_hs_grad_level calc and stu_hs_grad_year …
queryResults.querySql:
/*Changes made by  Syeravadekar-  09-15-2021
Adding filter for contact_type, fix for missing state values and missing stu_hs_grad_level calc and stu_hs_grad_year values and making it swap compliant
ESDP 746, 747, 692,
 757
-- made changes to populate partner_id from school_panto_id to school_panto_guid
-- Made changes to Null out the international addresses
*/
--Madhvi v1.0 10/29/2021 Remove duplicates from xwalk

select  distinct  NULLIF(TRIM(Con.first_name), '')   as   firstname,
  NULLIF(TRIM(Con.last_name), '')   as   lastname,
  TRIM(Con.email_address)   as   email,
  case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' AND scca.cass_success_ind = true AND
  (
	CONCAT
	(
		COALESCE(Con.first_name,''),
		COALESCE(Con.last_name,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.addr_1,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.addr_2,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.city,''),
		COALESCE(state_translation.eabstandard_value,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.country,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.ZIP5,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.zip4,''),
		COALESCE(CAST(Con.phone_number as varchar),'')
	) REGEXP '.*[^[:ascii:]].*') = FALSE
  then scca.addr_1 else null end   as   address1,
  --case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' then NULLIF(TRIM(SCCA.ADDR_1), '') else null end   as   address1,
  case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' then NULLIF(TRIM(SCCA.ADDR_2), '') else null end   as   address2,
  case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' then NULLIF(TRIM(SCCA.city), '') else null end   as   city,
  case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' then NULLIF(TRIM(state_translation.eabstandard_value), '') else null end   as   state,
  TRIM(case when INITCAP(SCCA.country) = 'Unknown' or lower(SCCA.country) = 'unmapped value' then null else SCCA.country end)   as   country,
  CASE 
		WHEN NULLIF(SCCA.zip5,'') IS NOT NULL AND NULLIF(SCCA.zip4,'') IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(CONCAT(SCCA.zip5,'-' ,SCCA.zip4) AS varchar(64))
		WHEN NULLIF(SCCA.zip5,'') IS NOT NULL AND NULLIF(SCCA.zip4,'') IS NULL THEN CAST(SCCA.zip5 as varchar(64))
    	ELSE CAST(SCCA.POSTAL_CD as varchar(64))
  END AS zipcode,
  --TRIM(case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' then SCCA.ZIP5 else null end)   as   zipcode,
  TRIM(SCCA.CREATE_DT)   as   CREATE_DTS,
  TRIM(Con.phone_number)   as   mobile,
  TRIM(Con.distance_from_campus)   as   dist_from_campus_calc,
  TRIM(AC.is_deleted)   as   is_deleted,
  TRIM(race_stdz.race)   as   race_stdzd,
  TRIM(Con.ethnicity)   as   ethnicity_stdzd,
  null   as   religion_partner,
  NULL AS academic_field_intrst_bln,
--  TRIM(ac_blnd.academic_interest_blnd)   as   academic_field_intrst_bln,
  TRIM(Con.contact_key)   as   eab_contact_id,
  NULLIF(TRIM(Con.contact_type_calc), '')   as   eab_contact_type,
  INITCAP(NULLIF(TRIM(Con.funnel_status_calc), ''))   as   funnel_stage_calc,
  TRIM(AC.student_application_status)   as   student_app_status,
  TRIM(AC.form_student_first_name)   as   form_student_first_name,
  TRIM(AC.form_student_last_name)   as   form_student_last_name,
  TRIM(AC.form_parent_first_name)   as   form_parent_first_name,
  TRIM(AC.form_parent_last_name)   as   form_parent_last_name,
  TRIM(AC.form_parent_email)   as   form_parent_email,
  TRIM(AC.form_referred_by_EAB_ID)   as   form_referred_by_EAB_ID,
  TRIM(label.source_label)   as   og_contact_source_calc,
  TRIM(all_source.all_sources_blnd)   as   all_sources_blnd,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_NAME)   as   form_h_school_name,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_ADDR)   as   form_h_school_addr,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_CITY)   as   form_h_school_city,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_STATEPROV)   as   form_h_school_stateprov,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_POST_CODE)   as   form_h_school_post_code,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_COUNTRY)   as   form_h_school_country,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_GRAD_YEAR)   as   form_h_school_grad_year,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_ENTRY_YEAR)   as   form_entry_year,
  TRIM(Con.current_grade_level)   as   h_school_grade_level_calc,
  TRIM(Con.grad_year)   as   h_school_grad_year_calc,
  TRIM(max_values.sat_max)   as   max_sat_score_rng_calc,
  TRIM(max_values.act_max)   as   max_act_score_rng_calc,
  TRIM(max_values.psat_max)   as   max_psat_score_rng_calc,
  TRIM(max_values.preact_max)   as   max_preact_score_rng_calc,
  null   as   fafsa_submit_date_partner,
  TRIM(Con.contact_rand)   as   random_number,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_BOT_HONEYPOT)   as   form_bot_honeypot,
  case when AC.ACS_REPLICATION_DATE IS NOT NULL then CONCAT(LEFT(REPLACE(TRIM(AC.ACS_REPLICATION_DATE), ' ', 'T'), 19), '+00:00') else null end   as   acs_replication_date,
  TRIM(xwalk.print_display_id)   as   print_display_id,
  TRIM(PD.PANTO_SCHOOL_GUID)   as   es_partner_id,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_ACADEMIC_FIELD_INTRS)   as   Form_Academic_Field_Intrs,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_EMAIL_UPDATE_CONTACT_KEY)   as   FORM_EMAIL_UPDATED_EAB_ID,
  TRIM(AC.Form_Student_Addr)   as   FORM_STUDENT_ADDR,
  TRIM(AC.Form_Student_City)   as   FORM_STUDENT_CITY,
  TRIM(AC.Form_Student_Stateprov)   as   form_student_stateprov,
  TRIM(AC.Form_Student_Post_Code)   as   form_student_post_code,
  TRIM(AC.Form_Student_Country)   as   form_student_country,
  TRIM(AC.Form_Sms_Opt_In)   as   form_sms_opt_in,
  TRIM(AC.Engaged_Inq_Cmpgn_Acsl)   as   engaged_inq_cmpgn_acsl,
  TRIM(AC.Engaged_Reeng_Cmpgn_Acsl)   as   engaged_reeng_cmpgn_acsl,
  TRIM(parent.FIRST_NAME)   as   child_first_name_calc,
  TRIM(parent.LAST_NAME)   as   child_last_name_calc,
  TRIM(case when Con.suppress_mail_ind = 1 then 'Y' else 'N' end)   as   do_not_direct_mail_calc,
  case when lower(optin_sms_indicator) = 'false' then 'false' when lower(optin_sms_indicator) = 'true' then 'true' else null end   as   sms_opt_in_calc,
  TRIM(case when Con.suppress_email_ind = 1 then 'TRUE' else 'FALSE' end)   as   dnc_email,
  null   as   dnc_email_comment,
  PHN.optin_sms_indicator,
  case when Con.contact_type_calc = 'Parent/Guardian' then parent.stu_hs_grade_level_calc else Con.current_grade_level end   as   stu_hs_grade_level_calc,
  TRIM(Con.grad_year)   as   high_school_grad_year_calculated,
  null   as   student_funnel_stage_calc,
  INITCAP(NULLIF(TRIM(parent.student_funnel_stage_calc), ''))   as   stu_funnel_stage_calc,
  TRIM(AC.student_application_status)   as   stu_eab_app_status,
  NULL AS stu_aca_field_intrst_blnd,
--  TRIM(ac_blnd.academic_interest_blnd)   as   stu_aca_field_intrst_blnd,
  TRIM(race_stdz.race)   as   stu_race_stdzd,
  TRIM(Con.ethnicity)   as   stu_ethnicity_stdzd,
  null   as   stu_religion_partner,
  case when Con.contact_type_calc = 'Parent/Guardian' then parent.high_school_grad_year_calculated else Con.grad_year end   as   stu_hs_grad_year_calc,
  ac.eng_app_par_gen_acsl   as   eng_app_par_gen_acsl,
  ac.eng_app_stu_gen_acsl   as   eng_app_stu_gen_acsl,
  ac.eng_app_stu_paper_acsl   as   eng_app_stu_paper_acsl,
  ac.eng_app_stu_sub_acsl   as   eng_app_stu_sub_acsl,
  ac.eng_cul_par_inq_acsl   as   eng_cul_par_inq_acsl,
  ac.eng_cul_par_nur_acsl   as   eng_cul_par_nur_acsl,
  ac.eng_cul_stu_inq_acsl   as   eng_cul_stu_inq_acsl,
  ac.eng_cul_stu_paper_acsl   as   eng_cul_stu_paper_acsl,
  ac.eng_cul_stu_nur_acsl   as   eng_cul_stu_nur_acsl,
  ac.eng_cul_stu_reen_acsl   as   eng_cul_stu_reen_acsl,
  ac.eng_cul_stu_j_reen_acsl   as   eng_cul_stu_j_reen_acsl,
  ac.eng_cul_stu_sms_acsl   as   eng_cul_stu_sms_acsl,
  ac.st_dt_app_par_gen_acsl   as   st_dt_app_par_gen_acsl,
  ac.st_dt_app_stu_gen_acsl   as   st_dt_app_stu_gen_acsl,
  ac.st_dt_app_stu_paper_acsl   as   st_dt_app_stu_paper_acsl,
  ac.st_dt_cul_par_inq_acsl   as   st_dt_cul_par_inq_acsl,
  ac.st_dt_cul_par_nur_acsl   as   st_dt_cul_par_nur_acsl,
  ac.st_dt_cul_stu_inq_acsl   as   st_dt_cul_stu_inq_acsl,
  ac.st_dt_cul_stu_paper_acsl   as   st_dt_cul_stu_paper_acsl,
  ac.st_dt_cul_stu_nur_acsl   as   st_dt_cul_stu_nur_acsl,
  ac.st_dt_cul_stu_j_reen_acsl   as   st_dt_cul_stu_j_reen_acsl,
  ac.st_dt_cul_stu_reen_acsl   as   st_dt_cul_stu_reen_acsl,
  ac.st_dt_cul_stu_sms_acsl   as   st_dt_cul_stu_sms_acsl 
 
from   PDP.con__contact_assigned as Con left join PDP.add__sourcecontact_clean_addr as SCCA on Con.CLEAN_ADDR_KEY = SCCA.CLEAN_ADDR_KEY
Left join ( SELECT distinct Contact_key, dummy_email,
acs_contact_id,print_display_id
			  FROM (
					  SELECT  CAC.CONTACT_KEY Contact_key, CAC.DUMMY_EMAIL dummy_email, CAC.ACS_CONTACT_ID acs_contact_id,CAC.print_display_id,
							  row_number() over (partition by CAC.CONTACT_KEY order by CAC.CREATE_DT asc) rnum
					FROM PDP.prc__contact_acquia_xwalk as CAC
					) as xw where xw.rnum=1 ) as xwalk 
on con.Contact_key = xwalk.Contact_key
left join PDP.acs__contacts as AC on xwalk.acs_contact_id = AC.acs_contact_id left join  <[Partner_Data_Platform].[Phone]>  as PHN on PHN.phone_number = Con.phone_number left join (
select   Con.FIRST_NAME,
  Con.LAST_NAME,
  Con.CONTACT_KEY 
from   PDP.con__contact_assigned as Con left join PDP.con__contact_relations as d on Con.CONTACT_KEY = d.student_contact_key 
where  initcap(Con.contact_type_calc) = 'Parent/Guardian'
) as child_names on child_names.CONTACT_KEY = Con.CONTACT_KEY left join (
select   CTS_PIVOT.contact_key   as   contact_key,
  CTS_PIVOT.sourcecontact_id   as   sourcecontact_id,
  max(sat_max)   as   sat_max,
  max(act_max)   as   act_max,
  max(psat_max)   as   psat_max,
  max(preact_max)   as   preact_max 
from   (
select   CTS.contact_key   as   contact_key,
  CTS.sourcecontact_id,
  case when UPPER(CTS.test_type) = 'SAT' then CTS.score_range_max else null end   as   sat_max,
  case when UPPER(CTS.test_type) = 'ACT' then CTS.score_range_max else null end   as   act_max,
  case when UPPER(CTS.test_type) = 'PSAT' then CTS.score_range_max else null end   as   psat_max,
  case when UPPER(CTS.test_type) = 'PREACT' then CTS.score_range_max else null end   as   preact_max 
from   PDP.con__contact_test_scores as CTS 
) as CTS_PIVOT 
group by   CTS_PIVOT.contact_key, CTS_PIVOT.sourcecontact_id 
) as max_values on Con.contact_key = max_values.contact_key and Con.active_sourcecontact_id = max_values.sourcecontact_id left join  <[Partner_Data_Platform].[Sourcecontact Sourcetype]>  as srccontact_srctype on srccontact_srctype. <Source Contact ID>  = Con.active_sourcecontact_id left join pdp.crf__intake_type as srctype on srccontact_srctype. <Source Type Key>  = srctype.intake_type_key left outer join es_pdp_common.common.common_source_standard_mappings as state_translation on UPPER(state_translation.source_type) = 'GENERAL' and Upper(state_translation.Category) = 'STATE' and Lower(state_translation.SOURCE_FIELD_NAME) = 'state' and lower(state_translation.source_code) = lower(SCCA.state) left join (
select   a.contact_key,
  LISTAGG(a.eab_std_value, '|')   as   academic_interest_blnd 
from   (
select  distinct  b.contact_key,
  b.eab_std_value,
  b.attribute_type 
from   PDP.con__contact_attributes_combined as b 
) as a 
where  Lower(a.attribute_type) = 'academic_interest'
group by   a.contact_key 
) as ac_blnd on Con.contact_key = ac_blnd.contact_key left join (
select   a.contact_key,
  a.sourcecontact_id,
  LISTAGG(a.eab_std_value, '|')   as   race 
from   (
select  distinct  b.contact_key,
  b.sourcecontact_id,
  b.eab_std_value,
  b.attribute_type 
from   PDP.con__contact_attributes_combined as b 
) as a 
where  Lower(a.attribute_type) = 'race'
group by   a.contact_key, a.sourcecontact_id 
) as race_stdz on Con.contact_key = race_stdz.contact_key and Con.active_sourcecontact_id = race_stdz.sourcecontact_id left join (
select   list_sources.contact_key,
  LISTAGG(list_sources.all_source_bln_list_agg, '|')   as   all_sources_blnd 
from   (
select   contact_key,
  case when lower(intake_type_label) = 'prenames' then 'Migrated Contact' else null end   as   all_source_bln_list_agg 
from   PDP.crf__contact_sourcecontacts as CSCS left join pdp.crf__intake_type as intake on CSCS.source_type_key = intake.intake_type_key 
where  LOWER(CSCS.active_ind) = 'true' and lower(intake_type_label) = 'prenames'
 UNION 
select  distinct  contact_key,
  source_label   as   all_source_bln_list_agg 
from   PDP.crf__contact_sourcecontacts as CSCS inner join pdp.crf__source as srctype on CSCS.source_key = srctype.source_key 
where  LOWER(CSCS.active_ind) = 'true'
) as list_sources 
group by   list_sources.contact_key 
) as all_source on Con.contact_key = all_source.contact_key left join (
select   con3.first_name,
  con3.last_name,
  con3.parent_contact_key,
  con3.student_contact_key,
  con3.stu_hs_grade_level_calc   as   stu_hs_grade_level_calc,
  con3.high_school_grad_year_calculated   as   high_school_grad_year_calculated,
  con3.student_funnel_stage_calc   as   student_funnel_stage_calc 
from   (
select  distinct  con2.first_name,
  con2.last_name,
  con2.parent_contact_key,
  con2.student_contact_key,
  con2.stu_hs_grade_level_calc   as   stu_hs_grade_level_calc,
  con2.high_school_grad_year_calculated   as   high_school_grad_year_calculated,
  con2.student_funnel_stage_calc   as   student_funnel_stage_calc,
  row_number() over (partition by con2.parent_contact_key order by  con2.sourcecontact_intake_dt   ASC )   as   rankid2 
from   (
select  distinct  rel.parent_contact_key,
  rel.student_contact_key,
  scst.create_date   as   sourcecontact_intake_dt,
  con1.current_grade_level   as   stu_hs_grade_level_calc,
  con1.grad_year   as   high_school_grad_year_calculated,
  con1.first_name,
  con1.last_name,
  con1.funnel_status_calc   as   student_funnel_stage_calc,
  row_number() over (partition by rel.parent_contact_key order by  int.INTAKE_PRIORITY   ASC )   as   rankid 
from   PDP.con__contact_assigned as con inner join PDP.crf__contact_sourcecontacts as src on con.contact_key = src.contact_key inner join pdp.crf__intake_type as int on int.intake_type_key = src.source_type_key inner join  <[Partner_Data_Platform].[SourceContact SourceType]>  as scst on src.sourcecontact_id = scst.source_contact_id left join PDP.con__contact_relations as rel on rel.parent_contact_key = con.contact_key left join PDP.con__contact_assigned as con1 on rel.student_contact_key = con1.contact_key 
where  con.contact_type_calc = 'Parent/Guardian'
) as con2 
where  rankid = 1
) as con3 
where  rankid2 = 1
) as parent on Con.contact_key = parent.parent_contact_key left join (
select   sub_1.contact_key,
  sub_1.source_label   as   source_label 
from   (
select   ROW_NUMBER() over (partition by contact_key order by  CSCTS.create_dt   ASC )   as   row_id,
  CSCTS.contact_key,
  srctype.source_label 
from   PDP.crf__contact_sourcecontacts as CSCTS inner join pdp.crf__source as srctype on CSCTS.source_key = srctype.source_key 
) as sub_1 
where  row_id = 1
) as label on Con.contact_key = label.contact_key inner join PDP.prc__partner_details as PD 

 where (NULLIF(TRIM(Con.contact_type_calc ), '')   in  ('Student','Parent/Guardian', 'Ride Along','Deliverability Seed')and ((TRIM(label.source_label) is not null and TRIM(all_source.all_sources_blnd) is not null)) and lower(Con.email_address ) not like '%test.eab.com') or (NULLIF(TRIM(Con.contact_type_calc ), '') in ('Deliverability Seed', 'Ride Along') and TRIM(all_source.all_sources_blnd) is null and lower(Con.email_address ) not like '%test.eab.com')

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

/*Changes made by Shruti-
Adding filter for contact_type, fix for missing state values and missing stu_hs_grad_level calc and stu_hs_grad_year values and making it swap compliant
ESDP 746, 747, 692 , 757
-- made changes to populate partner_id from school_panto_id to school_panto_guid
-- Made changes to Null out the international addresses
Shunter added filter for duplicate contact keys and duplicate emails
*/



select  distinct  NULLIF(TRIM(Con.first_name), '')   as   firstname ,  NULLIF(TRIM(Con.last_name), '')   as   lastname ,  TRIM(Con.email_address )   as   email ,  Case When Lower(SCCA.country ) = 'united states' 
	 Then NULLIF(TRIM(SCCA.ADDR_1), '') 
	 Else Null 
	 End as   address1 ,
Case When Lower(SCCA.country ) = 'united states'
     Then NULLIF(TRIM(SCCA.ADDR_2), '') 
	 Else Null
	 End as   address2 , 
Case When Lower(SCCA.country ) = 'united states'
     Then NULLIF(TRIM(SCCA. city ), '') 
	 Else Null
	 End as   city ,  
Case When Lower(SCCA.country ) = 'united states'
     Then NULLIF(TRIM(state_translation.eabstandard_value), '')  
	 Else Null
	 End as   state ,
 TRIM(case when INITCAP(SCCA.country ) = 'Unknown' or lower(SCCA.country ) = 'unmapped value' then null else SCCA.country  end)   as   country ,
 TRIM(case when Lower(SCCA.country ) = 'united states' then SCCA.ZIP5 else null end)   as   zipcode ,  TRIM(SCCA.CREATE_DT)   as   CREATE_DTS ,
 TRIM(Con.phone_number )   as   mobile ,  TRIM(Con.distance_from_campus)   as   dist_from_campus_calc ,  TRIM(AC.is_deleted) as is_deleted ,  TRIM(race_stdz.race)   as   race_stdzd
 ,  TRIM(Con.ethnicity )   as   ethnicity_stdzd ,  null   as   religion_partner ,  TRIM(ac_blnd.academic_interest_blnd)   as   academic_field_intrst_bln ,
 TRIM(Con. contact_key)   as   eab_contact_id ,  NULLIF(TRIM(Con.contact_type_calc ), '')   as   eab_contact_type ,  INITCAP(NULLIF(TRIM(Con.funnel_status_calc ), ''))
 as   funnel_stage_calc ,  TRIM(AC.student_application_status )   as   student_app_status ,  TRIM(AC.form_student_first_name )   as   form_student_first_name ,
 TRIM(AC. form_student_last_name )   as   form_student_last_name ,  TRIM(AC.form_parent_first_name )   as   form_parent_first_name ,  TRIM(AC. form_parent_last_name)
 as   form_parent_last_name ,  TRIM(AC.form_parent_email)   as   form_parent_email ,  TRIM(AC.form_referred_by_EAB_ID )   as   form_referred_by_EAB_ID ,  TRIM(label.source_label)   as   og_contact_source_calc ,  TRIM(all_source.all_sources_blnd)   as   all_sources_blnd ,  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_NAME)   as   form_h_school_name ,  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_ADDR)   as   form_h_school_addr ,  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_CITY)   as   form_h_school_city ,  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_STATEPROV)   as   form_h_school_stateprov ,  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_POST_CODE)   as   form_h_school_post_code ,  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_COUNTRY)   as   form_h_school_country ,  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_GRAD_YEAR)   as   form_h_school_grad_year ,  TRIM(AC.FORM_ENTRY_YEAR)   as   form_entry_year ,  TRIM(Con.current_grade_level)   as   h_school_grade_level_calc ,  TRIM(Con.grad_year)   as   h_school_grad_year_calc ,  TRIM(max_values.sat_max)   as   max_sat_score_rng_calc ,  TRIM(max_values.act_max)   as   max_act_score_rng_calc ,  TRIM(max_values.psat_max)   as   max_psat_score_rng_calc ,  TRIM(max_values.preact_max)   as   max_preact_score_rng_calc ,  null   as   fafsa_submit_date_partner ,  TRIM(Con.contact_rand)   as   random_number ,  TRIM(AC.FORM_BOT_HONEYPOT)   as   form_bot_honeypot ,  case when AC.ACS_REPLICATION_DATE IS NOT NULL then CONCAT(LEFT(REPLACE(TRIM(AC.ACS_REPLICATION_DATE), ' ', 'T'), 19), '+00:00') else null end   as   acs_replication_date ,  TRIM(CAC.print_display_id )   as   print_display_id , setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

queryResults.sqlPreview: /*Changes made by Syeravadekar- 09-15-2021 Adding filter for contact_type, fix for missing state values and missing stu_hs_grad_level calc and stu_hs_grad_year …
queryResults.querySql:
/*Changes made by  Syeravadekar-  09-15-2021
Adding filter for contact_type, fix for missing state values and missing stu_hs_grad_level calc and stu_hs_grad_year values and making it swap compliant
ESDP 746, 747, 692,
 757
-- made changes to populate partner_id from school_panto_id to school_panto_guid
-- Made changes to Null out the international addresses
*/
--Madhvi v1.0 10/29/2021 Remove duplicates from xwalk
--Shunter 11/16/21 Filtered out duplicate emails



select  distinct  NULLIF(TRIM(Con.first_name), '')   as   firstname,
  NULLIF(TRIM(Con.last_name), '')   as   lastname,
  TRIM(Con.email_address)   as   email,
  case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' AND scca.cass_success_ind = true AND
	(
	  CONCAT
		(
		COALESCE(Con.first_name,''),
		COALESCE(Con.last_name,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.addr_1,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.addr_2,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.city,''),
		COALESCE(state_translation.eabstandard_value,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.country,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.ZIP5,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.zip4,''),
		COALESCE(CAST(Con.phone_number as varchar),'')
		) REGEXP '.*[^[:ascii:]].*') = FALSE
	then scca.addr_1 else null end   as   address1,
  case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' then NULLIF(TRIM(SCCA.ADDR_2), '') else null end   as   address2,
  case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' then NULLIF(TRIM(SCCA.city), '') else null end   as   city,
  case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' then NULLIF(TRIM(state_translation.eabstandard_value), '') else null end   as   state,
  TRIM(case when INITCAP(SCCA.country) = 'Unknown' or lower(SCCA.country) = 'unmapped value' then null else SCCA.country end)   as   country,
  CASE 
	WHEN NULLIF(SCCA.zip5,'') IS NOT NULL AND NULLIF(SCCA.zip4,'') IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(CONCAT(SCCA.zip5,'-' ,SCCA.zip4) AS varchar(64))
	WHEN NULLIF(SCCA.zip5,'') IS NOT NULL AND NULLIF(SCCA.zip4,'') IS NULL THEN CAST(SCCA.zip5 as varchar(64))
    ELSE CAST(SCCA.POSTAL_CD as varchar(64))
  END AS zipcode,
  --TRIM(case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' AND length(SCCA.ZIP5) = 5 then SCCA.zip5 else null end) as zipcode,
  TRIM(SCCA.CREATE_DT)   as   CREATE_DTS,
  TRIM(Con.phone_number)   as   mobile,
  TRIM(Con.distance_from_campus)   as   dist_from_campus_calc,
  TRIM(AC.is_deleted)   as   is_deleted,
  TRIM(race_stdz.race)   as   race_stdzd,
  TRIM(Con.ethnicity)   as   ethnicity_stdzd,
  null   as   religion_partner,
  NULL as academic_field_intrst_bln,
  --TRIM(ac_blnd.academic_interest_blnd)   as   academic_field_intrst_bln,
  TRIM(Con.contact_key)   as   eab_contact_id,
  NULLIF(TRIM(Con.contact_type_calc), '')   as   eab_contact_type,
  INITCAP(NULLIF(TRIM(Con.funnel_status_calc), ''))   as   funnel_stage_calc,
  TRIM(AC.student_application_status)   as   student_app_status,
  TRIM(AC.form_student_first_name)   as   form_student_first_name,
  TRIM(AC.form_student_last_name)   as   form_student_last_name,
  TRIM(AC.form_parent_first_name)   as   form_parent_first_name,
  TRIM(AC.form_parent_last_name)   as   form_parent_last_name,
  TRIM(AC.form_parent_email)   as   form_parent_email,
  TRIM(AC.form_referred_by_EAB_ID)   as   form_referred_by_EAB_ID,
  TRIM(label.source_label)   as   og_contact_source_calc,
  TRIM(all_source.all_sources_blnd)   as   all_sources_blnd,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_NAME)   as   form_h_school_name,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_ADDR)   as   form_h_school_addr,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_CITY)   as   form_h_school_city,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_STATEPROV)   as   form_h_school_stateprov,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_POST_CODE)   as   form_h_school_post_code,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_COUNTRY)   as   form_h_school_country,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_GRAD_YEAR)   as   form_h_school_grad_year,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_ENTRY_YEAR)   as   form_entry_year,
  TRIM(Con.current_grade_level)   as   h_school_grade_level_calc,
  TRIM(Con.grad_year)   as   h_school_grad_year_calc,
  TRIM(max_values.sat_max)   as   max_sat_score_rng_calc,
  TRIM(max_values.act_max)   as   max_act_score_rng_calc,
  TRIM(max_values.psat_max)   as   max_psat_score_rng_calc,
  TRIM(max_values.preact_max)   as   max_preact_score_rng_calc,
  null   as   fafsa_submit_date_partner,
  TRIM(Con.contact_rand)   as   random_number,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_BOT_HONEYPOT)   as   form_bot_honeypot,
  case when AC.ACS_REPLICATION_DATE IS NOT NULL then CONCAT(LEFT(REPLACE(TRIM(AC.ACS_REPLICATION_DATE), ' ', 'T'), 19), '+00:00') else null end   as   acs_replication_date,
  TRIM(xwalk.print_display_id)   as   print_display_id,
  TRIM(PD.PANTO_SCHOOL_GUID)   as   es_partner_id,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_ACADEMIC_FIELD_INTRS)   as   Form_Academic_Field_Intrs,
  TRIM(AC.FORM_EMAIL_UPDATE_CONTACT_KEY)   as   FORM_EMAIL_UPDATED_EAB_ID,
  TRIM(AC.Form_Student_Addr)   as   FORM_STUDENT_ADDR,

where  initcap(Con.contact_type_calc) = 'Parent/Guardian'
) as child_names on child_names.CONTACT_KEY = Con.CONTACT_KEY left join (
select   CTS_PIVOT.contact_key   as   contact_key,
  CTS_PIVOT.sourcecontact_id   as   sourcecontact_id,
  max(sat_max)   as   sat_max,
  max(act_max)   as   act_max,
  max(psat_max)   as   psat_max,
  max(preact_max)   as   preact_max 
from   (
select   CTS.contact_key   as   contact_key,
  CTS.sourcecontact_id,
  case when UPPER(CTS.test_type) = 'SAT' then CTS.score_range_max else null end   as   sat_max,
  case when UPPER(CTS.test_type) = 'ACT' then CTS.score_range_max else null end   as   act_max,
  case when UPPER(CTS.test_type) = 'PSAT' then CTS.score_range_max else null end   as   psat_max,
  case when UPPER(CTS.test_type) = 'PREACT' then CTS.score_range_max else null end   as   preact_max 
from   PDP.con__contact_test_scores as CTS 
) as CTS_PIVOT 
group by   CTS_PIVOT.contact_key, CTS_PIVOT.sourcecontact_id 
) as max_values on Con.contact_key = max_values.contact_key and Con.active_sourcecontact_id = max_values.sourcecontact_id left join  <[Partner_Data_Platform].[Sourcecontact Sourcetype]>  as srccontact_srctype on srccontact_srctype. <Source Contact ID>  = Con.active_sourcecontact_id left join pdp.crf__intake_type as srctype on srccontact_srctype. <Source Type Key>  = srctype.intake_type_key left outer join es_pdp_common.common.common_source_standard_mappings as state_translation on UPPER(state_translation.source_type) = 'GENERAL' and Upper(state_translation.Category) = 'STATE' and Lower(state_translation.SOURCE_FIELD_NAME) = 'state' and lower(state_translation.source_code) = lower(SCCA.state) left join (
select   a.contact_key,
  LISTAGG(a.eab_std_value, '|')   as   academic_interest_blnd 
from   (
select  distinct  b.contact_key,
  b.eab_std_value,
  b.attribute_type 
from   PDP.con__contact_attributes_combined as b 
) as a 
where  Lower(a.attribute_type) = 'academic_interest'
group by   a.contact_key 
) as ac_blnd on Con.contact_key = ac_blnd.contact_key left join (
select   a.contact_key,
  a.sourcecontact_id,
  LISTAGG(a.eab_std_value, '|')   as   race 
from   (
select  distinct  b.contact_key,
  b.sourcecontact_id,
  b.eab_std_value,
  b.attribute_type 
from   PDP.con__contact_attributes_combined as b 
) as a 
where  Lower(a.attribute_type) = 'race'
group by   a.contact_key, a.sourcecontact_id 
) as race_stdz on Con.contact_key = race_stdz.contact_key and Con.active_sourcecontact_id = race_stdz.sourcecontact_id left join (
select   list_sources.contact_key,
  LISTAGG(list_sources.all_source_bln_list_agg, '|')   as   all_sources_blnd 
from   (
select   contact_key,
  case when lower(intake_type_label) = 'prenames' then 'Migrated Contact' else null end   as   all_source_bln_list_agg 
from   PDP.crf__contact_sourcecontacts as CSCS left join pdp.crf__intake_type as intake on CSCS.source_type_key = intake.intake_type_key 
where  LOWER(CSCS.active_ind) = 'true' and lower(intake_type_label) = 'prenames'
 UNION 
select  distinct  contact_key,

from   PDP.crf__contact_sourcecontacts as CSCS inner join pdp.crf__source as srctype on CSCS.source_key = srctype.source_key

  con3.high_school_grad_year_calculated   as   high_school_grad_year_calculated,
  con3.student_funnel_stage_calc   as   student_funnel_stage_calc 
from   (

  con2.student_contact_key,

  con2.student_funnel_stage_calc   as   student_funnel_stage_calc,
  row_number() over (partition by con2.parent_contact_key order by  con2.sourcecontact_intake_dt   ASC )   as   rankid2 
from   (
select  distinct  rel.parent_contact_key,
  rel.student_contact_key,
  scst.create_date   as   sourcecontact_intake_dt,
  con1.current_grade_level   as   stu_hs_grade_level_calc,

  row_number() over (partition by rel.parent_contact_key order by  int.INTAKE_PRIORITY   ASC )   as   rankid 
from   PDP.con__contact_assigned as con inner join PDP.crf__contact_sourcecontacts as src on con.contact_key = src.contact_key inner join pdp.crf__intake_type as int on int.intake_type_key = src.source_type_key inner join  <[Partner_Data_Platform].[SourceContact SourceType]>  as scst on src.sourcecontact_id = scst.source_contact_id left join PDP.con__contact_relations as rel on rel.parent_contact_key = con.contact_key left join PDP.con__contact_assigned as con1 on rel.student_contact_key = con1.contact_key 
where  con.contact_type_calc = 'Parent/Guardian'

where  rankid = 1

where  rankid2 = 1

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

max(CTS_PIVOT.psat_max) as psat_max,
max(CTS_PIVOT.preact_max) as preact_max
from (
select CTS.<Contact Key> as contact_key,CTS.<Source Contact ID> as sourcecontact_id,
case when UPPER(CTS.<Test Type>)='SAT' then CTS.<Score Range Maximum>  else null  end as sat_max, 
case when UPPER(CTS.<Test Type>)='ACT' then CTS.<Score Range Maximum>  else null end as act_max,
case when UPPER(CTS.<Test Type>)='PSAT' then CTS.<Score Range Maximum>  else null  end as psat_max,

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

queryResults.sqlPreview: /*Changes made by Syeravadekar- 09-15-2021 Adding filter for contact_type, fix for missing state values and missing stu_hs_grad_level calc and stu_hs_grad_year …
queryResults.querySql:
/*Changes made by  Syeravadekar-  09-15-2021
Adding filter for contact_type, fix for missing state values and missing stu_hs_grad_level calc and stu_hs_grad_year values and making it swap compliant
ESDP 746, 747, 692 , 757
-- made changes to populate partner_id from school_panto_id to school_panto_guid
-- Made changes to Null out the international addresses
*/
--Madhvi v1.0 10/29/2021 Remove duplicates from xwalk


select  distinct  
NULLIF(TRIM(Con.first_name), '')   as   firstname ,  
NULLIF(TRIM(Con.last_name), '')   as   lastname ,  
TRIM(Con.email_address)   as   email ,  
case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' AND scca.cass_success_ind = true AND
	(
	  CONCAT
		(
		COALESCE(Con.first_name,''),
		COALESCE(Con.last_name,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.addr_1,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.addr_2,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.city,''),
		COALESCE(state_translation.eabstandard_value,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.country,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.ZIP5,''),
		COALESCE(SCCA.zip4,''),
		COALESCE(CAST(Con.phone_number as varchar),'')
		) REGEXP '.*[^[:ascii:]].*') = FALSE
	then scca.addr_1 else null end   as   address1,
--case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' then NULLIF(TRIM(SCCA.ADDR_1), '') else null end   as   address1 ,  
case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' then NULLIF(TRIM(SCCA.ADDR_2), '') else null end   as   address2 ,  
case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' then NULLIF(TRIM(SCCA.city), '') else null end   as   city ,  
case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' then NULLIF(TRIM(state_translation.eabstandard_value), '') else null end   as   state ,  
TRIM(case when INITCAP(SCCA.country) = 'Unknown' or lower(SCCA.country) = 'unmapped value' then null else SCCA.country end)   as   country ,  
CASE 
	WHEN NULLIF(SCCA.zip5,'') IS NOT NULL AND NULLIF(SCCA.zip4,'') IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(CONCAT(SCCA.zip5,'-' ,SCCA.zip4) AS varchar(64))
	WHEN NULLIF(SCCA.zip5,'') IS NOT NULL AND NULLIF(SCCA.zip4,'') IS NULL THEN CAST(SCCA.zip5 as varchar(64))
    ELSE CAST(SCCA.POSTAL_CD as varchar(64))
END AS zipcode,
--TRIM(case when Lower(SCCA.country) = 'united states' then SCCA.ZIP5 else null end)   as   zipcode ,  
TRIM(SCCA.CREATE_DT)   as   CREATE_DTS ,  
TRIM(Con.phone_number)   as   mobile ,  
TRIM(Con.distance_from_campus)   as   dist_from_campus_calc ,  
TRIM(AC.is_deleted)   as   is_deleted ,  
TRIM(race_stdz.race)   as   race_stdzd ,  
TRIM(Con.ethnicity)   as   ethnicity_stdzd ,  
null   as   religion_partner ,  
TRIM(ac_blnd.academic_interest_blnd)   as   academic_field_intrst_bln ,  
TRIM(Con.contact_key)   as   eab_contact_id ,  
NULLIF(TRIM(Con.contact_type_calc), '')   as   eab_contact_type ,  
INITCAP(NULLIF(TRIM(Con.funnel_status_calc), ''))   as   funnel_stage_calc ,  
TRIM(AC.student_application_status)   as   student_app_status ,  
TRIM(AC.form_student_first_name)   as   form_student_first_name ,  
TRIM(AC.form_student_last_name)   as   form_student_last_name ,  
TRIM(AC.form_parent_first_name)   as   form_parent_first_name ,  
TRIM(AC.form_parent_last_name)   as   form_parent_last_name ,  
TRIM(AC.form_parent_email)   as   form_parent_email ,  
TRIM(AC.form_referred_by_EAB_ID)   as   form_referred_by_EAB_ID ,  
TRIM(label.source_label)   as   og_contact_source_calc ,  
TRIM(all_source.all_sources_blnd)   as   all_sources_blnd ,  
TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_NAME)   as   form_h_school_name ,  
TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_ADDR)   as   form_h_school_addr ,  
TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_CITY)   as   form_h_school_city ,  
TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_STATEPROV)   as   form_h_school_stateprov ,  
TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_POST_CODE)   as   form_h_school_post_code ,  
TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_COUNTRY)   as   form_h_school_country ,  
TRIM(AC.FORM_H_SCHOOL_GRAD_YEAR)   as   form_h_school_grad_year ,  
TRIM(AC.FORM_ENTRY_YEAR)   as   form_entry_year ,  
TRIM(Con.current_grade_level)   as   h_school_grade_level_calc ,  
TRIM(Con.grad_year)   as   h_school_grad_year_calc ,  
TRIM(max_values.sat_max)   as   max_sat_score_rng_calc ,  
TRIM(max_values.act_max)   as   max_act_score_rng_calc ,  
TRIM(max_values.psat_max)   as   max_psat_score_rng_calc ,  
TRIM(max_values.preact_max)   as   max_preact_score_rng_calc ,  
null   as   fafsa_submit_date_partner ,  
TRIM(Con.contact_rand)   as   random_number ,  
TRIM(AC.FORM_BOT_HONEYPOT)   as   form_bot_honeypot ,  
case when AC.ACS_REPLICATION_DATE IS NOT NULL then CONCAT(LEFT(REPLACE(TRIM(AC.ACS_REPLICATION_DATE), ' ', 'T'), 19), '+00:00') else null end   as   acs_replication_date ,
TRIM(xwalk.print_display_id)   as   print_display_id ,  
TRIM(PD.PANTO_SCHOOL_GUID)   as   es_partner_id ,  
TRIM(AC.FORM_ACADEMIC_FIELD_INTRS)   as   Form_Academic_Field_Intrs ,  
TRIM(AC.FORM_EMAIL_UPDATE_CONTACT_KEY)   as   FORM_EMAIL_UPDATED_EAB_ID ,  
TRIM(AC.Form_Student_Addr)   as   FORM_STUDENT_ADDR ,  
TRIM(AC.Form_Student_City)   as   FORM_STUDENT_CITY ,  
TRIM(AC.Form_Student_Stateprov)   as   form_student_stateprov ,  
TRIM(AC.Form_Student_Post_Code)   as   form_student_post_code ,  
TRIM(AC.Form_Student_Country)   as   form_student_country ,  
TRIM(AC.Form_Sms_Opt_In)   as   form_sms_opt_in ,  
TRIM(AC.Engaged_Inq_Cmpgn_Acsl)   as   engaged_inq_cmpgn_acsl ,  
TRIM(AC.Engaged_Reeng_Cmpgn_Acsl)   as   engaged_reeng_cmpgn_acsl ,  
TRIM(parent.FIRST_NAME)   as   child_first_name_calc ,  
TRIM(parent.LAST_NAME)   as   child_last_name_calc ,  
TRIM(case when Con.suppress_mail_ind = 1 then 'Y' else 'N' end)   as   do_not_direct_mail_calc ,  
case when lower(optin_sms_indicator) = 'false' then 'false' when lower(optin_sms_indicator) = 'true' then 'true' else null end   as   sms_opt_in_calc ,  
TRIM(case when Con.suppress_email_ind = 1 then 'TRUE' else 'FALSE' end)   as   dnc_email ,  
null   as   dnc_email_comment ,  
PHN.optin_sms_indicator ,  
case when Con.contact_type_calc = 'Parent/Guardian' then parent.stu_hs_grade_level_calc else Con.current_grade_level end   as   stu_hs_grade_level_calc ,
TRIM(Con.grad_year)   as   high_school_grad_year_calculated ,  
null   as   student_funnel_stage_calc ,  
INITCAP(NULLIF(TRIM(parent.student_funnel_stage_calc), ''))   as   stu_funnel_stage_calc ,  
TRIM(AC.student_application_status)   as   stu_eab_app_status ,  
TRIM(ac_blnd.academic_interest_blnd)   as   stu_aca_field_intrst_blnd ,  
TRIM(race_stdz.race)   as   stu_race_stdzd ,  
TRIM(Con.ethnicity)   as   stu_ethnicity_stdzd ,  
null   as   stu_religion_partner ,  
case when Con.contact_type_calc = 'Parent/Guardian' then parent.high_school_grad_year_calculated else Con.grad_year end   as   stu_hs_grad_year_calc ,
ac.eng_app_par_gen_acsl   as   eng_app_par_gen_acsl ,  
ac.eng_app_stu_gen_acsl   as   eng_app_stu_gen_acsl ,  
ac.eng_app_stu_paper_acsl   as   eng_app_stu_paper_acsl ,  
ac.eng_app_stu_sub_acsl   as   eng_app_stu_sub_acsl ,  
ac.eng_cul_par_inq_acsl   as   eng_cul_par_inq_acsl ,  
ac.eng_cul_par_nur_acsl   as   eng_cul_par_nur_acsl ,  
ac.eng_cul_stu_inq_acsl   as   eng_cul_stu_inq_acsl ,  
ac.eng_cul_stu_paper_acsl   as   eng_cul_stu_paper_acsl ,  
ac.eng_cul_stu_nur_acsl   as   eng_cul_stu_nur_acsl ,

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

WITH last_delivered_cte AS (
    SELECT MAX(log_del.contact_deleted_dt) AS last_del
    FROM PDP_ALR_V2.log__acs_contact_deletions AS log_del -- Latest deletion date already sent to Acquia

SELECT
    CAST(ead.es_partner_id AS VARCHAR(64)) AS es_partner_id,
    CAST(ead.acs_contact_id AS VARCHAR(50)) AS acs_contact_id
FROM <[Acquia_ALR].[exp__acquia_deletions].{fulfillment}> AS ead
CROSS JOIN last_delivered_cte
WHERE CASE
    WHEN last_delivered_cte.last_del IS NULL THEN 1 = 1 -- First run: send all fulfillment rows
    ELSE ead.contact_deleted_dt > last_delivered_cte.last_del -- Later runs: send only newer deletions
END

queryResults.sqlPreview: /* This bound query delivers to the exp__acquia_gdpr_hard_delete_requests entity in the Acquia_ALR domain. Records identified here have already been soft delete…
queryResults.querySql:
/*
This bound query delivers to the exp__acquia_gdpr_hard_delete_requests
entity in the Acquia_ALR domain.

Records identified here have already been soft deleted for GDPR by the
ALR GDPR soft-delete process. This BQ identifies those records that have
passed the required retention period and sends the ACS contact ID to
Acquia for permanent hard deletion.
*/

WITH acs_contacts AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(gdpr_acs.contact_key AS VARCHAR(50)) AS eab_contact_id,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.acs_contact_id AS INT) AS acs_contact_id,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.email AS VARCHAR(64)) AS email,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.is_deleted AS BOOLEAN) AS is_deleted,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.is_deleted_dt AS TIMESTAMP) AS is_deleted_dt,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.is_deleted_reason AS VARCHAR(64)) AS is_deleted_reason,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.contact_identifier_hash AS VARCHAR(255)) AS contact_identifier_hash,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.es_partner_id AS VARCHAR(50)) AS es_partner_id
    FROM <[PDP_ALR_V2].[gdpr__acs_record_deletion].{final}> AS gdpr_acs
    WHERE LOWER(gdpr_acs.is_deleted) = 'true'
      AND gdpr_acs.is_deleted_reason = 'GDPR'
)

SELECT
    ac.es_partner_id,
    ac.acs_contact_id
FROM acs_contacts AS ac

INNER JOIN es_pdp_common.common.REF__DELETION_REQUESTS AS del_req
    ON del_req.contact_identifier_hash = ac.contact_identifier_hash
   AND LOWER(del_req.mes_business_line) = 'alr'
   AND del_req.voided_dt IS NULL
   AND del_req.voided_by IS NULL
   AND del_req.void_source IS NULL
   AND (DATEDIFF(DAY,CAST(ac.is_deleted_dt AS DATE),CURRENT_DATE()) >= 14 AND MOD(DATEDIFF(DAY,CAST(ac.is_deleted_dt AS DATE),CURRENT_DATE()),14) = 0);

queryResults.sqlPreview: /* This bound query delivers to the exp__acquia_gdpr_soft_delete_requests entity in Acquia_ALR domain Once the record is GDPRd, we no longer identify it in PDP …
queryResults.querySql:
/*
This bound query delivers to the exp__acquia_gdpr_soft_delete_requests entity in Acquia_ALR domain
Once the record is GDPRd, we no longer identify it in PDP and before permanently deleting that record in Acquia_ALR, we have to set it for soft delete i.e., is_deleted = 1
So this BQ identifies the GDPRd records that are still in the files recevived back from replication and set them for soft deletion.
If the record is already marked is_deleted = 1, we no longer send it to Acquia
*/


WITH
-- Get all the contacts which aren't soft deleted yet
acs_contacts AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(acs_con.contact_key AS VARCHAR(50)) AS eab_contact_id,
        CAST(acs_con.acs_contact_id AS INT) AS acs_contact_id,
        CAST(acs_con.email AS VARCHAR(64)) AS email,
		CAST(acs_con.is_deleted AS BOOLEAN) AS is_deleted,
		CAST(acs_con.date_added AS TIMESTAMP) AS rec_added_dt,
	    CAST(acs_con.contact_identifier_hash AS VARCHAR) AS contact_identifier_hash,
		CAST(acs_con.es_partner_id AS VARCHAR) AS es_partner_id,
        CAST(acs_con.acs_replication_date AS timestamp) AS acs_replication_date							  
    FROM <[PDP_ALR_V2].[gdpr__acs_record_deletion].{final}>  AS acs_con
	WHERE (acs_con.is_deleted IS NULL OR lower(acs_con.is_deleted) = 'false' OR (lower(acs_con.is_deleted) = 'true' AND (acs_con.is_deleted_reason IS NULL OR acs_con.is_deleted_reason <> 'GDPR'))) -- record is not yet set to is_deleted = true
		

)
SELECT
    ac.es_partner_id,
    ac.eab_contact_id,
    ac.email,
    TO_VARCHAR(CONCAT(SPLIT_PART(REPLACE(TO_TIMESTAMP(CAST(ac.acs_replication_date AS STRING),'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS.FF'),' ','T'),'.',0),'+00:00')) AS acs_replication_date,
    '1' AS is_deleted,
    TO_VARCHAR(CONCAT(SPLIT_PART(REPLACE(CONVERT_TIMEZONE('America/New_York', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()),' ','T'),'.',0),'+00:00')) AS is_deleted_dt,
    'GDPR' AS is_deleted_reason
FROM acs_contacts AS ac
INNER JOIN es_pdp_common.common.REF__DELETION_REQUESTS AS del_req
        ON del_req.contact_identifier_hash = ac.contact_identifier_hash
       AND LOWER(del_req.mes_business_line) = 'alr'
       AND (del_req.voided_dt IS NULL AND del_req.voided_by IS NULL AND del_req.void_source IS NULL) -- GDPR request for the contact_identifier_hash is not reverted/voided
	   AND DATE(del_req.CREATE_DT) >= CURRENT_DATE - 30
	   AND DATE(del_req.CREATE_DT) > ac.rec_added_dt -- Set as soft delete only if the contact in ACS is created before we had the GDPR request

queryResults.querySql:
-- Delivers contact deletions to ACS, limited to deletions not yet sent
WITH last_delivered_cte AS (
    -- Latest deletion date already sent to ACS
    SELECT
        MAX(log_del.contact_deleted_dt) AS last_del
    FROM PDP_AMS.log__acs_contact_deletions AS log_del
)

SELECT
    CAST(ead.<ES Partner ID> AS varchar(64)) AS es_partner_id,
    CAST(ead.<ACS Contact ID> AS varchar(50)) AS acs_contact_id
FROM <[Acquia_AMS].[exp__acquia_deletions].{fulfillment}> AS ead
CROSS JOIN last_delivered_cte -- Single-row CTE, so this only exposes last_del to the filter
WHERE
    CASE
        -- First delivery to ACS: no prior deletions logged, so send everything

queryResults.querySql:
/*
This bound query delivers to the exp__acquia_gdpr_hard_delete_requests entity in Acquia_AMS domain
Records here were already soft deleted (is_deleted = 1, reason = GDPR) by the soft delete BQ in a prior cycle
This BQ identifies those soft-deleted records that are now past the retention window and sends only the acs_contact_id back to Acquia so the record can be permanently (hard) deleted
*/

-- Get all the contacts already soft deleted due to GDPR, matched to GDPR deletion requests
WITH acs_contacts AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<Contact Key> AS VARCHAR(50)) AS eab_contact_id,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<ACS Contact ID> AS INT) AS acs_contact_id,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<Email> AS VARCHAR(64)) AS email,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<Is Deleted> AS BOOLEAN) AS is_deleted,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<Is Deleted Dt> AS TIMESTAMP) AS is_deleted_dt,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<Is Deleted Reason> AS VARCHAR(64)) AS is_deleted_reason,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<Contact Identifier Hash> AS VARCHAR(255)) AS contact_identifier_hash,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<ES Partner Id> AS VARCHAR(50)) AS es_partner_id
    FROM <[PDP_AMS].[gdpr__acs_record_deletion].{final}> AS gdpr_acs
    WHERE (lower(gdpr_acs.is_deleted) = 'true' AND gdpr_acs.is_deleted_reason = 'GDPR') -- record is already set to is_deleted = true
)

SELECT
    ac.es_partner_id,
    ac.acs_contact_id -- only the acs_contact_id is needed for Acquia to hard delete the record
FROM acs_contacts AS ac
INNER JOIN es_pdp_common.common.REF__DELETION_REQUESTS AS del_req
    ON del_req.contact_identifier_hash = ac.contact_identifier_hash
   AND LOWER(del_req.mes_business_line) = 'ams'
   AND (del_req.voided_dt IS NULL AND del_req.voided_by IS NULL AND del_req.void_source IS NULL) -- GDPR request for the contact_identifier_hash is not reverted/voided
   AND (DATEDIFF(DAY, CAST(ac.is_deleted_dt AS DATE), CURRENT_DATE()) >= 14 AND (MOD(DATEDIFF(DAY, CAST(ac.is_deleted_dt AS DATE), CURRENT_DATE()), 14) = 0)) -- only send for hard delete once, at least 14 days after soft delete, on a 14-day cadence

queryResults.sqlPreview: /* This bound query delivers to the exp__acquia_gdpr_soft_delete_requests entity in Acquia_AMS domain Once the record is GDPRd, we no longer identify it in PDP …
queryResults.querySql:
/*
This bound query delivers to the exp__acquia_gdpr_soft_delete_requests entity in Acquia_AMS domain
Once the record is GDPRd, we no longer identify it in PDP and before permanently deleting that record in Acquia_AMS, we have to set it for soft delete i.e., is_deleted = 1
So this BQ identifies the GDPRd records that are still in the files recevived back from replication and set them for soft deletion.
If the record is already marked is_deleted = 1, we no longer send it to Acquia
*/


-- Get all the contacts which aren't soft deleted yet, matched to GDPR deletion requests
WITH acs_contacts AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<Contact Key> AS varchar(50)) AS eab_contact_id,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<ACS Contact ID> AS int) AS acs_contact_id,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<Email> AS varchar(64)) AS email,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<Is Deleted> AS boolean) AS is_deleted,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<Date Added> AS timestamp) AS rec_added_dt,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<Contact Identifier Hash> AS varchar) AS contact_identifier_hash,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<ES Partner Id> AS varchar) AS es_partner_id,
        CAST(gdpr_acs.<ACS Replication Date> AS timestamp) AS acs_replication_date
    FROM <[PDP_AMS].[gdpr__acs_record_deletion].{final}> AS gdpr_acs
	WHERE (gdpr_acs.is_deleted IS NULL OR lower(gdpr_acs.is_deleted) = 'false' OR (lower(gdpr_acs.is_deleted) = 'true' AND (gdpr_acs.is_deleted_reason IS NULL OR gdpr_acs.is_deleted_reason <> 'GDPR'))) -- record is not yet set to is_deleted = true
)

SELECT
    ac.es_partner_id,
    ac.eab_contact_id,
    ac.email,
    TO_VARCHAR(CONCAT(SPLIT_PART(REPLACE(TO_TIMESTAMP(CAST(ac.acs_replication_date AS STRING),'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS.FF'),' ','T'),'.',0),'+00:00')) AS acs_replication_date,
    '1' AS is_deleted,
    TO_VARCHAR(CONCAT(SPLIT_PART(REPLACE(CONVERT_TIMEZONE('America/New_York', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()),' ','T'),'.',0),'+00:00')) AS is_deleted_dt,
    'GDPR' AS is_deleted_reason
FROM acs_contacts AS ac
INNER JOIN es_pdp_common.common.REF__DELETION_REQUESTS AS del_req
        ON del_req.contact_identifier_hash = ac.contact_identifier_hash
       AND LOWER(del_req.mes_business_line) = 'ams'
       AND (del_req.voided_dt IS NULL AND del_req.voided_by IS NULL AND del_req.void_source IS NULL) -- GDPR request for the contact_identifier_hash is not reverted/voided
	   AND DATE(del_req.CREATE_DT) >= CURRENT_DATE - 30
	   AND DATE(del_req.CREATE_DT) > ac.rec_added_dt -- Set as soft delete only if the contact in ACS is created before we had the GDPR request

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

WHEN MONTH(TRY_TO_DATE(a.ADMIT_DATE)) = 12 THEN 'DECEMBER'
ELSE NULL END ANALYSIS_CUSTOM_FIELD_2
,CASE

WHEN MONTH(TRY_TO_DATE(a.ENROLL_DATE)) = 2 THEN 'FEBRUARY'

WHEN MONTH(TRY_TO_DATE(a.ENROLL_DATE)) = 6 THEN 'JUNE'
WHEN MONTH(TRY_TO_DATE(a.ENROLL_DATE)) = 7 THEN 'JULY'
WHEN MONTH(TRY_TO_DATE(a.ENROLL_DATE)) = 8 THEN 'AUGUST'
WHEN MONTH(TRY_TO_DATE(a.ENROLL_DATE)) = 9 THEN 'SEPTEMBER'
WHEN MONTH(TRY_TO_DATE(a.ENROLL_DATE)) = 10 THEN 'OCTOBER'
WHEN MONTH(TRY_TO_DATE(a.ENROLL_DATE)) = 11 THEN 'NOVEMBER'
WHEN MONTH(TRY_TO_DATE(a.ENROLL_DATE)) = 12 THEN 'DECEMBER'
ELSE NULL END ANALYSIS_CUSTOM_FIELD_3
,a.ANALYSIS_CUSTOM_FIELD_4
,a.ANALYSIS_CUSTOM_FIELD_5
,CASE 
WHEN LEFT(a.GENERIC_STAGING_FIELD_02,1) IN ('5','6','7','8','9')  AND TO_NUMBER(CASE 
WHEN TRY_TO_DATE(a.APPLICATION_SUBMIT_DATE) BETWEEN '2021-07-01' AND '2022-06-30' OR TRY_TO_DATE(a.ADMIT_DATE) BETWEEN '2021-07-01' AND '2022-06-30' THEN 2022

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.
