setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

reasons: Parse time improved in 5.1.4 (5.0.0-3 1081ms · 5.1.4 559ms (5.1.4 faster by 522ms))

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

reasons: Parse time improved in 5.1.4 (5.0.0-3 455ms · 5.1.4 338ms (5.1.4 faster by 117ms))

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

reasons: Parse time improved in 5.1.4 (5.0.0-3 457ms · 5.1.4 338ms (5.1.4 faster by 119ms))

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

reasons: Parse time improved in 5.1.4 (5.0.0-3 474ms · 5.1.4 355ms (5.1.4 faster by 119ms))

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

reasons: Parse time improved in 5.1.4 (5.0.0-3 353ms · 5.1.4 288ms (5.1.4 faster by 65ms))

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

queryResults.sqlPreview: WITH base AS ( -- unique students per Entry Year/Term/Type SELECT st.eab_entry_year_academic, st.eab_entry_term, st.eab_student_type, st.primary_student_id, MAX…
queryResults.querySql:
WITH base AS (  -- unique students per Entry Year/Term/Type
    SELECT
        st.eab_entry_year_academic,
        st.eab_entry_term,
        st.eab_student_type,
        st.primary_student_id,
        MAX(CASE WHEN st.eab_inquiry_ind = 'true' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS inquiry_flag
    FROM <[ALR].[Student Program].{final}> st
    GROUP BY
        st.eab_entry_year_academic,
        st.eab_entry_term,
        st.eab_student_type,
        st.primary_student_id
),
apps AS (  -- app rollup (includes NULL keys)
    SELECT
        sta.eab_entry_year_academic,
        sta.eab_entry_term,
        sta.eab_student_type,
        SUM(CASE WHEN sta.eab_app_start_ind      = 'true' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Started_Applications,
        SUM(CASE WHEN sta.eab_app_incomplete_ind = 'true' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Submitted_Applications,
        SUM(CASE WHEN sta.eab_app_complete_ind   = 'true' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Completed_Applications,
        SUM(CASE WHEN sta.eab_admit_ind          = 'true' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Admits,
        SUM(CASE WHEN sta.eab_cond_admit_ind     = 'true' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Conditional_Admits,
        SUM(CASE WHEN sta.eab_deny_ind           = 'true' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Denies,
        SUM(CASE WHEN sta.eab_deposit_ind        = 'true' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Deposits,
        SUM(CASE WHEN sta.eab_withdrawal_ind     = 'true' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Withdrawals,
        SUM(CASE WHEN sta.eab_enroll_ind         = 'true' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Enrolls
    FROM <[ALR].[Student Term Application].{final}> sta
    GROUP BY
        sta.eab_entry_year_academic,
        sta.eab_entry_term,
        sta.eab_student_type
)
SELECT
    COALESCE(b.eab_entry_year_academic, a.eab_entry_year_academic) AS Entry_Year,
    COALESCE(b.eab_entry_term,          a.eab_entry_term)          AS Entry_Term,
    COALESCE(b.eab_student_type,        a.eab_student_type)        AS Student_Type,

    COUNT(DISTINCT b.primary_student_id)                                          AS Prospects,
    SUM(CASE WHEN b.inquiry_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                           AS Inquiries,

    COALESCE(a.Started_Applications,   0)                                         AS Started_Applications,
    COALESCE(a.Submitted_Applications, 0)                                         AS Submitted_Applications,
    COALESCE(a.Completed_Applications, 0)                                         AS Completed_Applications,
    COALESCE(a.Admits,                 0)                                         AS Admits,
    COALESCE(a.Conditional_Admits,     0)                                         AS Conditional_Admits,
    COALESCE(a.Denies,                 0)                                         AS Denies,
    COALESCE(a.Deposits,               0)                                         AS Deposits,
    COALESCE(a.Withdrawals,            0)                                         AS Withdrawals,
    COALESCE(a.Enrolls,                0)                                         AS Enrolls,

    SUM(CASE WHEN b.primary_student_id IS NOT NULL AND s.EAB_OPT_OUT_IND = 'true'
             THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                                                  AS General_OptOuts,
	SUM(CASE WHEN b.primary_student_id IS NOT NULL AND s.EAB_EMAIL_OPTOUT_IND = 'true'
             THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                                                  AS Email_OptOuts
FROM base b
LEFT JOIN <[ALR].[Student].{final}> s
  ON s.primary_student_id = b.primary_student_id
FULL OUTER JOIN apps a
  ON (
        (b.eab_entry_year_academic = a.eab_entry_year_academic
         OR (b.eab_entry_year_academic IS NULL AND a.eab_entry_year_academic IS NULL))
    AND (b.eab_entry_term          = a.eab_entry_term
         OR (b.eab_entry_term IS NULL          AND a.eab_entry_term IS NULL))
    AND (b.eab_student_type        = a.eab_student_type
         OR (b.eab_student_type IS NULL        AND a.eab_student_type IS NULL))
  )
GROUP BY
    COALESCE(b.eab_entry_year_academic, a.eab_entry_year_academic),
    COALESCE(b.eab_entry_term,          a.eab_entry_term),
    COALESCE(b.eab_student_type,        a.eab_student_type),
    a.Started_Applications,
    a.Submitted_Applications,
    a.Completed_Applications,
    a.Admits,
    a.Conditional_Admits,
    a.Denies,
    a.Deposits,
    a.Withdrawals,
    a.Enrolls
ORDER BY
    Entry_Year,
    Entry_Term,
    Student_Type;

Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. stud.email_opt_out_indicator as email_optout_ind,
stud.phone_opt_out_indicator as phone_optout_ind,
stud.sms_opt_in_indicator as sms_optin_ind,
stud.sms_opt_out_indicator as sms_optout_ind,

case when pcm_email_optout_ind.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'

and coalesce(stud.mail_opt_out_indicator,'') = coalesce(pcm_mail_optout_ind.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[ALR].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_email_optout_ind
on (pcm_email_optout_ind.field_name = 'eab_email_optout_ind'
and coalesce(stud.email_opt_out_indicator,'') = coalesce(pcm_email_optout_ind.partner_value,''))

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

queryResults.querySql:
WITH
latest_applications AS (
    SELECT
        app_ranked.id AS id,
        app_ranked.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
        app_ranked.updated_at AS updated_at,
        app_ranked.created_at AS created_at,
        app_ranked.sis_student_id AS sis_student_id,
        app_ranked.first_name AS first_name,
        app_ranked.middle_name AS middle_name,
        app_ranked.last_name AS last_name,
        app_ranked.us_citizenship_status AS us_citizenship_status,
        app_ranked.international_indicator AS international_indicator,
        app_ranked.date_of_birth AS date_of_birth,
        app_ranked.gender AS gender,
        app_ranked.gender_identity AS gender_identity,
        app_ranked.religious_affiliation AS religious_affiliation,
        app_ranked.high_school_graduation_year AS high_school_graduation_year,
        app_ranked.first_generation_college AS first_generation_college,
        app_ranked.military_status AS military_status,
        app_ranked.alumni_relation_indicator AS alumni_relation_indicator,
        app_ranked.ethnicity AS ethnicity,
        app_ranked.campus_visit_count AS campus_visit_count,
        app_ranked.campus_visit_indicator AS campus_visit_indicator,
        app_ranked.first_campus_visit_date AS first_campus_visit_date,
        app_ranked.last_campus_visit_date AS last_campus_visit_date,
        app_ranked.ok_to_email AS ok_to_email,
        app_ranked.ok_to_call AS ok_to_call,
        app_ranked.ok_to_text AS ok_to_text
    FROM (
        SELECT
            app_src.id AS id,
            app_src.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
            app_src.updated_at AS updated_at,
            app_src.created_at AS created_at,
            app_src.sis_student_id AS sis_student_id,
            app_src.first_name AS first_name,
            app_src.middle_name AS middle_name,
            app_src.last_name AS last_name,
            app_src.us_citizenship_status AS us_citizenship_status,
            app_src.international_indicator AS international_indicator,
            app_src.date_of_birth AS date_of_birth,
            app_src.gender AS gender,
            app_src.gender_identity AS gender_identity,
            app_src.religious_affiliation AS religious_affiliation,
            app_src.high_school_graduation_year AS high_school_graduation_year,
            app_src.first_generation_college AS first_generation_college,
            app_src.military_status AS military_status,
            app_src.alumni_relation_indicator AS alumni_relation_indicator,
            app_src.ethnicity AS ethnicity,
            app_src.campus_visit_count AS campus_visit_count,
            app_src.campus_visit_indicator AS campus_visit_indicator,
            app_src.first_campus_visit_date AS first_campus_visit_date,
            app_src.last_campus_visit_date AS last_campus_visit_date,
            app_src.ok_to_email AS ok_to_email,
            app_src.ok_to_call AS ok_to_call,
            app_src.ok_to_text AS ok_to_text,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY app_src.prospect_id
                ORDER BY TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(app_src.updated_at) DESC NULLS LAST,
                TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(app_src.created_at) DESC NULLS LAST,
                TO_VARCHAR(app_src.id) DESC
            ) AS application_row_num
        FROM <[ECRM].[Applications].{fulfillment}> AS app_src
    ) AS app_ranked
    WHERE app_ranked.application_row_num = 1
),
activity_prospect_map AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(
            IFF(act_src.activitable_type ILIKE '%prospect%', NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(act_src.activitable_id)), ''), NULL),
            NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(app_for_act.prospect_id)), '')
        ) AS prospect_id,
        act_src.activity_type AS activity_type,
        act_src.description AS description,
        act_src.activity_date AS activity_date
    FROM <[ECRM].[Activities].{fulfillment}> AS act_src
    LEFT JOIN <[ECRM].[Applications].{fulfillment}> AS app_for_act
        ON NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(app_for_act.id)), '') = NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(act_src.activitable_id)), '')
       AND act_src.activitable_type ILIKE '%application%'
    WHERE COALESCE(
        IFF(act_src.activitable_type ILIKE '%prospect%', NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(act_src.activitable_id)), ''), NULL),
        NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(app_for_act.prospect_id)), '')
    ) IS NOT NULL
),
campus_visit_activity AS (
    SELECT
        apm.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
        COUNT(*) AS campus_visit_count_from_activities,
        MIN(TRY_TO_DATE(apm.activity_date)) AS first_campus_visit_date_from_activities,
        MAX(TRY_TO_DATE(apm.activity_date)) AS last_campus_visit_date_from_activities
    FROM activity_prospect_map AS apm
    WHERE apm.activity_type ILIKE '%campus%'
      AND (apm.activity_type ILIKE '%visit%' OR apm.description ILIKE '%visit%')
    GROUP BY apm.prospect_id
)
SELECT
    null as ALUMNI_RELATIONSHIP_EAB,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.alumni_relation_indicator)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.legacy_status)), '')) as ALUMNI_RELATIONSHIP_INDICATOR,
    TRY_TO_DATE(COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.date_of_birth)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.date_of_birth)), ''))) as BIRTH_DATE,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.id)), '') as CRM_STUDENT_ID,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_1,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_2,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_3,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_4,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_5,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_6,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_7,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_8,
    null as CALCULATED_ID_FIELD,
    cva.campus_visit_count_from_activities as CAMPUS_VISIT_COUNT,
    case when cva.campus_visit_count_from_activities > 0 then 'true' else 'false' end as CAMPUS_VISIT_INDICATOR,
    null as CAMPUS_VISIT_INDICATOR_EAB,
    null as EAB_STUDENT_ID,
    CASE
        WHEN COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_email)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_email)), '')) IS NULL THEN NULL
        WHEN CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_email)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_email)), '')) AS VARCHAR) = '0' then '1'
        WHEN CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_email)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_email)), '')) AS VARCHAR) = '1' then '0'
        ELSE NULL
    END as EMAIL_OPT_OUT_INDICATOR,
    null as EMAIL_OPT_OUT_INDICATOR_EAB,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ethnicity)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ethnicity)), '')) as ETHNICITY,
    null as ETHNICITY_EAB,
    cva.first_campus_visit_date_from_activities as FIRST_CAMPUS_VISIT_DATE,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.first_generation_college)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.first_generation_college)), '')) as FIRST_GENERATION_INDICATOR,
    null as FIRST_GENERATION_INDICATOR_EAB,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.first_name)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.first_name)), '')) as FIRST_NAME,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.gender)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.gender)), '')) as GENDER,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.high_school_graduation_year)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.high_school_graduation_year)), '')) as HIGH_SCHOOL_GRAD_YEAR,
    CASE
        WHEN COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ethnicity)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ethnicity)), '')) IS NULL THEN NULL
        WHEN COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ethnicity)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ethnicity)), '')) ILIKE '%hispanic%'
          OR COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ethnicity)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ethnicity)), '')) ILIKE '%latino%'
          OR COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ethnicity)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ethnicity)), '')) ILIKE '%latina%'
          OR COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ethnicity)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ethnicity)), '')) ILIKE '%latinx%'
        THEN 'TRUE'
        ELSE 'FALSE'
    END as HISPANIC_INDICATOR,
    p.intake_date as INTAKE_DATE,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.international_indicator)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.international_ind)), '')) as INTERNATIONAL_INDICATOR,
    null as INTERNATIONAL_INDICATOR_EAB,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.last_name)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.last_name)), '')) as LAST_NAME,
    CASE
        WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.mail_optout_ind)), '') IS NULL THEN NULL
        WHEN CAST(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.mail_optout_ind)), '') AS VARCHAR) = '0' then '1'
        WHEN CAST(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.mail_optout_ind)), '') AS VARCHAR) = '1' then '0'
        ELSE NULL
    END as MAIL_OPT_OUT_INDICATOR,
    null as MAIL_OPT_OUT_INDICATOR_EAB,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.middle_name)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.middle_name)), '')) as MIDDLE_NAME,
    null as MILITARY_SERVICE_OR_VETERAN_INDICATOR_EAB,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.military_status)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.military_status)), '')) as MILITARY_SERVICE_OR_VETERAN_STATUS,
    cva.last_campus_visit_date_from_activities as MOST_RECENT_CAMPUS_VISIT_DATE,
    CASE
        WHEN COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_email)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_email)), '')) IS NULL THEN NULL
        WHEN CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_email)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_email)), '')) AS VARCHAR) = '0' then '1'
        WHEN CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_email)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_email)), '')) AS VARCHAR) = '1' then '0'
        ELSE NULL
    END as OPT_OUT_INDICATOR_GENERAL,
    null as OPT_OUT_INDICATOR_GENERAL_EAB,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.PRIMARY_SOURCE)), '') as ORIGIN_SOURCE_CODE,
    TRY_TO_DATE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.created_at)), '')) as ORIGIN_SOURCE_DATE,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.external_id)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.sis_integration_id)), '')) as OTHER_STUDENT_ID,
    'navigate_crm_1' as PARTNER_SYSTEM_NAME,
    CASE
        WHEN COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_call)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_call)), '')) IS NULL THEN NULL
        WHEN CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_call)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_call)), '')) AS VARCHAR) = '0' then '1'
        WHEN CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_call)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_call)), '')) AS VARCHAR) = '1' then '0'
        ELSE NULL
    END as PHONE_OPT_OUT_INDICATOR,
    null as PHONE_OPT_OUT_INDICATOR_EAB,
    null as POPULATION_NAME,
    null as PREFERRED_FIRST_NAME,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.gender_identity)), ''),NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.gender)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.gender)), '')) as PREFERRED_GENDER,
    null as PREFERRED_GENDER_EAB,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.id)), '') as PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.religious_affiliation)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.religious_affiliation)), '')) as RELIGIOUS_AFFILIATION,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.sis_student_id)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.sis_student_id)), '')) as SIS_STUDENT_ID,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_text)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_text)), '')) as SMS_OPT_IN_INDICATOR,
    null as SMS_OPT_IN_INDICATOR_EAB,
    CASE
        WHEN COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_text)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_text)), '')) IS NULL THEN NULL
        WHEN CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_text)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_text)), '')) AS VARCHAR) = '0' then '1'
        WHEN CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_text)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_text)), '')) AS VARCHAR) = '1' then '0'

queryResults.sqlPreview: WITH latest_applications AS ( SELECT app_ranked.id AS id, app_ranked.prospect_id AS prospect_id, app_ranked.updated_at AS updated_at, app_ranked.created_at AS c…
queryResults.querySql:
WITH
latest_applications AS (
    SELECT
        app_ranked.id AS id,
        app_ranked.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
        app_ranked.updated_at AS updated_at,
        app_ranked.created_at AS created_at,
        app_ranked.sis_student_id AS sis_student_id,
        app_ranked.first_name AS first_name,
        app_ranked.middle_name AS middle_name,
        app_ranked.last_name AS last_name,
        app_ranked.us_citizenship_status AS us_citizenship_status,
        app_ranked.international_indicator AS international_indicator,
        app_ranked.date_of_birth AS date_of_birth,
        app_ranked.gender AS gender,
        app_ranked.gender_identity AS gender_identity,
        app_ranked.religious_affiliation AS religious_affiliation,
        app_ranked.high_school_graduation_year AS high_school_graduation_year,
        app_ranked.first_generation_college AS first_generation_college,
        app_ranked.military_status AS military_status,
        app_ranked.alumni_relation_indicator AS alumni_relation_indicator,
        app_ranked.ethnicity AS ethnicity,
        app_ranked.campus_visit_count AS campus_visit_count,
        app_ranked.campus_visit_indicator AS campus_visit_indicator,
        app_ranked.first_campus_visit_date AS first_campus_visit_date,
        app_ranked.last_campus_visit_date AS last_campus_visit_date,
        app_ranked.ok_to_email AS ok_to_email,
        app_ranked.ok_to_call AS ok_to_call,
        app_ranked.ok_to_text AS ok_to_text
    FROM (
        SELECT
            app_src.id AS id,
            app_src.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
            app_src.updated_at AS updated_at,
            app_src.created_at AS created_at,
            app_src.sis_student_id AS sis_student_id,
            app_src.first_name AS first_name,
            app_src.middle_name AS middle_name,
            app_src.last_name AS last_name,
            app_src.us_citizenship_status AS us_citizenship_status,
            app_src.international_indicator AS international_indicator,
            app_src.date_of_birth AS date_of_birth,
            app_src.gender AS gender,
            app_src.gender_identity AS gender_identity,
            app_src.religious_affiliation AS religious_affiliation,
            app_src.high_school_graduation_year AS high_school_graduation_year,
            app_src.first_generation_college AS first_generation_college,
            app_src.military_status AS military_status,
            app_src.alumni_relation_indicator AS alumni_relation_indicator,
            app_src.ethnicity AS ethnicity,
            app_src.campus_visit_count AS campus_visit_count,
            app_src.campus_visit_indicator AS campus_visit_indicator,
            app_src.first_campus_visit_date AS first_campus_visit_date,
            app_src.last_campus_visit_date AS last_campus_visit_date,
            app_src.ok_to_email AS ok_to_email,
            app_src.ok_to_call AS ok_to_call,
            app_src.ok_to_text AS ok_to_text,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY app_src.prospect_id
                ORDER BY TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(app_src.updated_at) DESC NULLS LAST,
                TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(app_src.created_at) DESC NULLS LAST,
                TO_VARCHAR(app_src.id) DESC
            ) AS application_row_num
        FROM <[ECRM].[Applications].{fulfillment}> AS app_src
    ) AS app_ranked
    WHERE app_ranked.application_row_num = 1
),
activity_prospect_map AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(
            IFF(act_src.activitable_type ILIKE '%prospect%', NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(act_src.activitable_id)), ''), NULL),
            NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(app_for_act.prospect_id)), '')
        ) AS prospect_id,
        act_src.activity_type AS activity_type,
        act_src.description AS description,
        act_src.activity_date AS activity_date
    FROM <[ECRM].[Activities].{fulfillment}> AS act_src
    LEFT JOIN <[ECRM].[Applications].{fulfillment}> AS app_for_act
        ON NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(app_for_act.id)), '') = NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(act_src.activitable_id)), '')
       AND act_src.activitable_type ILIKE '%application%'
    WHERE COALESCE(
        IFF(act_src.activitable_type ILIKE '%prospect%', NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(act_src.activitable_id)), ''), NULL),
        NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(app_for_act.prospect_id)), '')
    ) IS NOT NULL
),
campus_visit_activity AS (
    SELECT
        apm.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
        COUNT(*) AS campus_visit_count_from_activities,
        MIN(TRY_TO_DATE(apm.activity_date)) AS first_campus_visit_date_from_activities,
        MAX(TRY_TO_DATE(apm.activity_date)) AS last_campus_visit_date_from_activities
    FROM activity_prospect_map AS apm
    WHERE apm.activity_type ILIKE '%campus%'
      AND (apm.activity_type ILIKE '%visit%' OR apm.description ILIKE '%visit%')
    GROUP BY apm.prospect_id
)
SELECT
    null as ALUMNI_RELATIONSHIP_EAB,

        WHEN CAST(COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ok_to_email)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ok_to_email)), '')) AS VARCHAR) = '1' then '0'

        WHEN COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.ethnicity)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ethnicity)), '')) ILIKE '%hispanic%'

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

queryResults.querySql:
WITH
latest_applications AS (
    SELECT
        app_ranked.id AS id,
        app_ranked.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
        app_ranked.updated_at AS updated_at,
        app_ranked.created_at AS created_at,
        app_ranked.mailing_address_1 AS mailing_address_1,
        app_ranked.mailing_address_2 AS mailing_address_2,
        app_ranked.mailing_city AS mailing_city,
        app_ranked.mailing_state AS mailing_state,
        app_ranked.county AS county,
        app_ranked.mailing_zip AS mailing_zip,
        app_ranked.mailing_country AS mailing_country,
        app_ranked.permanent_address_1 AS permanent_address_1,
        app_ranked.permanent_address_2 AS permanent_address_2,
        app_ranked.permanent_city AS permanent_city,
        app_ranked.permanent_state AS permanent_state,
        app_ranked.permanent_zip AS permanent_zip,
        app_ranked.permanent_country AS permanent_country
    FROM (
        SELECT
            app_src.id AS id,
            app_src.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
            app_src.updated_at AS updated_at,
            app_src.created_at AS created_at,
            app_src.mailing_address_1 AS mailing_address_1,
            app_src.mailing_address_2 AS mailing_address_2,
            app_src.mailing_city AS mailing_city,
            app_src.mailing_state AS mailing_state,
            app_src.county AS county,
            app_src.mailing_zip AS mailing_zip,
            app_src.mailing_country AS mailing_country,
            app_src.permanent_address_1 AS permanent_address_1,
            app_src.permanent_address_2 AS permanent_address_2,
            app_src.permanent_city AS permanent_city,
            app_src.permanent_state AS permanent_state,
            app_src.permanent_zip AS permanent_zip,
            app_src.permanent_country AS permanent_country,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY app_src.prospect_id
                ORDER BY TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(app_src.updated_at) DESC NULLS LAST,
                TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(app_src.created_at) DESC NULLS LAST,
                TO_VARCHAR(app_src.id) DESC
            ) AS application_row_num
        FROM <[ECRM].[Applications].{fulfillment}> AS app_src
    ) AS app_ranked
    WHERE app_ranked.application_row_num = 1
)
SELECT
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.mailing_address_1)), '') AS "ADDRESS_LINE_1",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.mailing_address_2)), '') AS "ADDRESS_LINE_2",
    'Mailing' AS "ADDRESS_TYPE",
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_1,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_2,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_3,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_4,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_5,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_6,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_7,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_8,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_9,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.mailing_city)), '') AS "CITY",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.mailing_country)), '') AS "COUNTRY",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.mailing_country)), '') AS "COUNTRY_EAB",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.county)), '') AS "COUNTY",
	p.intake_date as INTAKE_DATE,
	p.intake_date as OBSERVATION_TIME,
	'navigate_crm_1' as PARTNER_SYSTEM_NAME,
	null as POPULATION_NAME,
	NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.id)), '') AS "PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID",																			
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.mailing_state)), '') AS "STATE_OR_PROVINCE",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.mailing_zip)), '') AS "ZIP_CODE"
FROM <[ECRM].[Prospects].{fulfillment}> AS p
<student_address_join_extension>																				 
WHERE COALESCE(
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.mailing_address_1)), ''),
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.mailing_city)), ''),
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.mailing_zip)), '')
) IS NOT NULL
and <student_address_where>
UNION
SELECT
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.permanent_address_1)), '') AS "ADDRESS_LINE_1",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.permanent_address_2)), '') AS "ADDRESS_LINE_2",
    'Permanent' AS "address_type",
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_1,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_2,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_3,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_4,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_5,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_6,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_7,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_8,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_9,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.permanent_city)), '') AS "CITY",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.permanent_country)), '') AS "COUNTRY",
    null AS "COUNTRY_EAB",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.county)), '') AS "COUNTY",
	p.intake_date as INTAKE_DATE,
	p.intake_date as OBSERVATION_TIME,
	'navigate_crm_1' as PARTNER_SYSTEM_NAME,
	null as POPULATION_NAME,
	NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.id)), '') AS "PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID",																			
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.permanent_state)), '') AS "STATE_OR_PROVINCE",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.permanent_zip)), '') AS "ZIP_CODE"
FROM <[ECRM].[Prospects].{fulfillment}> AS p
JOIN latest_applications AS la
    ON la.prospect_id = p.id

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

    stud.PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID as src_primary_student_id,
    'program' as src_attribute_type,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY 1) AS attribute_key,
	CASE
    WHEN stud.program IN ('Doctor of Nurse Anesthesia Practice (DNAP)', 'Master of Science in Biomedical Science') THEN 'hp_hsci'
	WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Science in Data Science') THEN 'hp_datatech'
	WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Science in Applied Artificial Intelligence (Pending HLC Accreditation)') THEN 'hp_datatech'
	WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Science in Applied Artificial Intelligence') THEN 'hp_datatech'
    WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Social Work') THEN 'hp_sbs'
	WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Science in Education') THEN 'hp_edu'
	WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Business Administration','Doctor of Business Administration') THEN 'hp_bus'
	WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Theology','Master of Theological Studies') THEN 'hp_rel'
    ELSE NULL end   as   dynamic_segment_name,
    '2026-01-15' as effective_dt,
    'dynamic_custom_segmentation' as eab_attribute_type,
	null as effective_end_date,
	s.INTAKE_DT as intake_dt,
	null as eab_std_value,
	null as eab_attribute_group
FROM <[ALR].[Student Program].{fulfillment}> stud
LEFT JOIN <[ALR].[Student].{fulfillment}> s
    ON stud.PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID = s.PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID
WHERE
    CASE
    WHEN stud.program IN ('Doctor of Nurse Anesthesia Practice (DNAP)', 'Master of Science in Biomedical Science') THEN 'hp_hsci'
	WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Science in Data Science') THEN ' hp_datatech'
	WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Science in Applied Artificial Intelligence (Pending HLC Accreditation)') THEN 'hp_datatech'
	WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Science in Applied Artificial Intelligence') THEN 'hp_datatech'
    WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Social Work') THEN 'hp_sbs'
	WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Science in Education') THEN 'hp_edu'
	WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Business Administration','Doctor of Business Administration') THEN 'hp_bus'
	WHEN stud.program IN ('Master of Theology','Master of Theological Studies') THEN 'hp_rel'
        ELSE NULL
    END IS NOT NULL

queryResults.sqlPreview: WITH latest_applications AS ( SELECT app_ranked.id AS id, app_ranked.prospect_id AS prospect_id, app_ranked.updated_at AS updated_at, app_ranked.created_at AS c…
queryResults.querySql:
WITH
latest_applications AS (
    SELECT
        app_ranked.id AS id,
        app_ranked.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
        app_ranked.updated_at AS updated_at,
        app_ranked.created_at AS created_at,
        app_ranked.primary_email AS primary_email
    FROM (
        SELECT
            app_src.id AS id,
            app_src.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
            app_src.updated_at AS updated_at,
            app_src.created_at AS created_at,
            app_src.primary_email AS primary_email,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY app_src.prospect_id
                ORDER BY TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(app_src.updated_at) DESC NULLS LAST,
                TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(app_src.created_at) DESC NULLS LAST,
                TO_VARCHAR(app_src.id) DESC
            ) AS application_row_num
        FROM <[ECRM].[Applications].{fulfillment}> AS app_src
    ) AS app_ranked
    WHERE app_ranked.application_row_num = 1
)
SELECT
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_1,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_2,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_3,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_4,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_5,
	null as CALCULATED_ID_FIELD,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.primary_email)), '') AS "EMAIL_ADDRESS",
	1 AS EMAIL_RANK,
	p.intake_date AS INTAKE_DT,
	'navigate_crm_1' AS PARTNER_SYSTEM_NAME,
	NULL AS POPULATION_NAME,
    NULL AS "EMAIL_TYPE",
    NULL AS "EMAIL_TYPE_EAB",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.id)), '') AS "PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID"
FROM <[ECRM].[Prospects].{fulfillment}> AS p
JOIN latest_applications AS la
    ON la.prospect_id = p.id
<student_email_join_extension>				
WHERE NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.primary_email)), '') IS NOT NULL
UNION
SELECT
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_1,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_2,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_3,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_4,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_5,
	null as CALCULATED_ID_FIELD,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.primary_email)), '') AS "EMAIL_ADDRESS",
	1 AS EMAIL_RANK,
	p.intake_date AS INTAKE_DT,
	'navigate_crm_1' AS PARTNER_SYSTEM_NAME,
	NULL AS POPULATION_NAME,
    NULL AS "EMAIL_TYPE",
    NULL AS "EMAIL_TYPE_EAB",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.id)), '') AS "PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID"
FROM <[ECRM].[Prospects].{fulfillment}> AS p
<student_email_join_extension>
WHERE NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.primary_email)), '') IS NOT NULL

queryResults.sqlPreview: WITH latest_applications AS ( SELECT app_ranked.id AS id, app_ranked.prospect_id AS prospect_id, app_ranked.updated_at AS updated_at, app_ranked.created_at AS c…
queryResults.querySql:
WITH
latest_applications AS (
    SELECT
        app_ranked.id AS id,
        app_ranked.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
        app_ranked.updated_at AS updated_at,
        app_ranked.created_at AS created_at,
        app_ranked.primary_phone AS primary_phone,
        app_ranked.primary_phone_type AS primary_phone_type,
        app_ranked.secondary_phone AS secondary_phone,
        app_ranked.secondary_phone_type AS secondary_phone_type
    FROM (
        SELECT
            app_src.id AS id,
            app_src.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
            app_src.updated_at AS updated_at,
            app_src.created_at AS created_at,
            app_src.primary_phone AS primary_phone,
            app_src.primary_phone_type AS primary_phone_type,
            app_src.secondary_phone AS secondary_phone,
            app_src.secondary_phone_type AS secondary_phone_type,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY app_src.prospect_id
                ORDER BY
                    TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(app_src.updated_at) DESC NULLS LAST,
                    TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(app_src.created_at) DESC NULLS LAST,
                    TO_VARCHAR(app_src.id) DESC
            ) AS application_row_num
        FROM <[ECRM].[Applications].{fulfillment}> AS app_src
    ) AS app_ranked
    WHERE app_ranked.application_row_num = 1
)

SELECT
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_1,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_2,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_3,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_4,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_5,
    null as CALCULATED_ID_FIELD,
    p.intake_date as INTAKE_DATE,
    'navigate_crm_1' as PARTNER_SYSTEM_NAME,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.primary_phone)), '') AS "PHONE_NUMBER",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.primary_phone_type)), '') AS "PHONE_NUMBER_TYPE",
    NULL AS "PHONE_NUMBER_TYPE_EAB",
    null as POPULATION_NAME,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.id)), '') AS "PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID"
FROM <[ECRM].[Prospects].{fulfillment}> AS p
<student_phone_join_extension>
WHERE NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.primary_phone)), '') IS NOT NULL
  AND <student_phone_where>

UNION ALL

SELECT
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_1,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_2,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_3,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_4,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_5,
    null as CALCULATED_ID_FIELD,
    p.intake_date as INTAKE_DATE,
    'navigate_crm_1' as PARTNER_SYSTEM_NAME,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.secondary_phone)), '') AS "PHONE_NUMBER",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.secondary_phone_type)), '') AS "PHONE_NUMBER_TYPE",
    NULL AS "PHONE_NUMBER_TYPE_EAB",
    null as POPULATION_NAME,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.id)), '') AS "PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID"
FROM <[ECRM].[Prospects].{fulfillment}> AS p
LEFT JOIN latest_applications AS la
    ON la.prospect_id = p.id
<student_phone_join_extension>
WHERE NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.secondary_phone)), '') IS NOT NULL
  AND <student_phone_where>

WITH
college_education AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(app.prospect_id)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.id)), '')) AS id,
        inst.ceeb_code AS ceeb_code,
        inst.name AS name,
        inst.city AS city,
        inst.state AS state,
        COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(aer.gpa)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(aer.cgpa)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.college_gpa)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.undergraduate_gpa)), '')) AS college_gpa_nbr,
        COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(aer.transfer_credits)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(aer.credits)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.transfer_credits)), '')) AS college_transfer_credits,
		p.intake_date
    FROM <[ECRM].[Application Education Records].{fulfillment}> AS aer
    JOIN <[ECRM].[Applications].{fulfillment}> AS app
        ON app.id = aer.application_id
    JOIN <[ECRM].[Prospects].{fulfillment}> AS p
        ON p.id = app.prospect_id
    JOIN <[ECRM].[Institutions].{fulfillment}> AS inst
        ON inst.id = aer.institution_id
    WHERE <student_prior_college_where>
)
SELECT
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_1,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_2,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_3,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_4,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_5,
	null as CALCULATED_ID_FIELD,
	p.intake_date as INTAKE_DATE,
	p.intake_date as OBSERVATION_TIME,
	'navigate_crm_1' as PARTNER_SYSTEM_NAME,
	null as POPULATION_NAME,
    p.id AS "PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.ceeb_code)), '') AS "UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_CEEB_CODE",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.city)), '') AS "UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_CITY",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.college_gpa_nbr)), '') AS "UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_GPA_NUMBER",
	NULL AS UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_MAJOR,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.name)), '') AS "UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_NAME",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.state)), '') AS "UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_STATE",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.college_transfer_credits)), '') AS "UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_TRANSFER_CREDITS"
FROM college_education AS p
<student_prior_college_join_extension>
WHERE p.id IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_1,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_2,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_3,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_4,
	null as CALCULATED_FIELD_5,
	null as CALCULATED_ID_FIELD,
	p.intake_date as INTAKE_DATE,
	p.intake_date as OBSERVATION_TIME,
	'navigate_crm_1' as PARTNER_SYSTEM_NAME,
	null as POPULATION_NAME,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.id)), '') AS "PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(inst.ceeb_code)), '') AS "UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_CEEB_CODE",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(inst.city)), '') AS "UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_CITY",
    COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.college_gpa)), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.undergraduate_gpa)), '')) AS "UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_GPA_NUMBER",
	NULL AS UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_MAJOR,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(inst.name)), '') AS "UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_NAME",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(inst.state)), '') AS "UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_STATE",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.transfer_credits)), '') AS "UNDERGRADUATE_INSTITUTION_TRANSFER_CREDITS"
FROM <[ECRM].[Prospects].{fulfillment}> AS p
JOIN <[ECRM].[Institutions].{fulfillment}> AS inst
    ON inst.id = p.last_college_id
<student_prior_college_join_extension>				
WHERE p.last_college_id IS NOT NULL
and <student_prior_college_where>

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.
