and try_cast(regexp_replace(ams_gifts_allocation_fulfillment.<fifth soft credit amount>,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float) >= 0

union

select
cast(ams_gifts_allocation_fulfillment.<gift id> as varchar) as gift_id,
cast(ams_gifts_allocation_fulfillment.<Calculated Field 1> as varchar) as soft_credit_id,
cast(ams_gifts_allocation_fulfillment.<gift allocation id> as varchar) as gift_allocation_id,
---cast(replace(replace(ams_gifts_allocation_fulfillment.<soft credit amount>, '$', ''),',','')  as float) as soft_credit_amount,
try_cast(regexp_replace(ams_gifts_allocation_fulfillment.<soft credit amount>,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float) as  soft_credit_amount,
cast(ams_gifts_allocation_fulfillment.<intake date> as timestamp) as intake_dt,
cast(ams_gifts_allocation_fulfillment.<gift date> as timestamp) as gift_dt,
cast(ams_gifts_allocation_fulfillment.<credit fiscal year> as varchar) as credit_fiscal_year
from <[AMS].[gifts_allocation].{fulfillment}> as ams_gifts_allocation_fulfillment
where try_cast(regexp_replace(ams_gifts_allocation_fulfillment.<Calculated Field 2>,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float) = 0
and ams_gifts_allocation_fulfillment.<soft credit id> is null
and  try_cast(regexp_replace(ams_gifts_allocation_fulfillment.<soft credit amount>,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float) >= 0
)
select distinct
ga.gift_id as gift_id,
ga.soft_credit_id as soft_credit_id,
ga.gift_allocation_id as gift_allocation_id,
row_number() over (partition by ga.gift_id order by ga.soft_credit_id desc, intake_dt desc) as soft_credit_sequence,
ga.soft_credit_amount as soft_credit_amount,
ga.intake_dt as intake_dt,
ga.gift_dt as gift_dt,
case when TO_NUMBER(ga.credit_fiscal_year) is null then gb.credited_fy
	 else TO_NUMBER(ga.credit_fiscal_year)
end as credit_fiscal_year,
case when
(MONTH(cast(getdate() as timestamp)) between <fy_month_1> and <fy_month_2>) then
	   YEAR(cast(getdate() as timestamp)) +1
			   else
			    YEAR(cast(getdate() as timestamp)) end  as  current_fiscal_year,
<source_partner_system_name_gifts_allocation> as source_partner_system_name,
<source_eab_system_type> as source_eab_system_type
from gifts_allocation as ga
join <fy_credited_gifts_allocation> as gb
on coalesce(ga.gift_id,'') = coalesce(gb.gift_id,'')
and coalesce(ga.soft_credit_id,'') = coalesce(gb.soft_credit_id,'')
--and try_cast(regexp_replace(gb.soft_credit_amount,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float) > 0
<join_extension_gifts_allocation>
						  
where ga.gift_id is not null
and ga.soft_credit_id is not null
and ga.soft_credit_amount is not null
and try_cast(regexp_replace(ga.soft_credit_amount,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float) > 0
order by ga.soft_credit_amount asc

with cte_credit_year as (
    select distinct
        gift_id,
        case
            when len(a.fy_credited) < 4 and a.fy_credited < 50 then to_number(concat(20,a.fy_credited))
            when len(a.fy_credited) < 4 and a.fy_credited > 50 then to_number(concat(19,a.fy_credited))
            else to_number(a.fy_credited)
        end as credited_fy
    from (
        select

                when giftmonth between <fy_month_1> and <fy_month_2> then giftyear + 1

            select
                cast(gs.<gift id> as varchar) as gift_id,
                gs.<gift date> as gift_date,
                month(cast(gs.<gift date> as timestamp)) as giftmonth,

queryResults.querySql:
with gifts_multiple_dates_single_funds as ( --CTE for gifts with multiple dates and single fund
select gift_id
from 
<[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g
where 1=1
and gift_id not in (select gift_id from <[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g group by gift_id having count(distinct src_donor_id)>1)
and gift_id not in (select gift_id from <[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g group by gift_id having count(distinct fund_code)>1)
group by gift_id having count(distinct gift_date)>1
)

,gifts_multiple_dates_multiple_funds as ( --CTE for gifts with multiple dates and multiple funds
select gift_id,gift_date,calculated_field_3 from ( 
select
gift_id,gift_date,calculated_field_3,row_number() over (partition by gift_id,gift_date order by calculated_field_3) as rn
from 
<[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g
where 1=1
and gift_id not in (select gift_id from <[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g group by gift_id having count(distinct src_donor_id)>1)
and gift_id in (select gift_id from <[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g group by gift_id having count(distinct fund_code)>1)
)gifts_multiple_dates_multiple_funds where rn=1
)

select 
gifts_funds.*
, <gifts_funds_eab_gift_is_annual_flag> as eab_gift_is_annual_flag
from 
(
select 
coalesce(gift_fund_id,case when gift_id in (select gift_id from gifts_multiple_dates_single_funds) then calculated_field_1 else gift_id end || fund_code || ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(fund_amount,'[^0-9.]', '') as float), 0)) as gift_fund_id
, case 
	when gift_id in (select gift_id from gifts_multiple_dates_single_funds) then calculated_field_1 --use gift key (bound to calculated field 1) for gift_id if gift_id present in list of gifts with multiple dates and single fund
	else gift_id 
  end as gift_id
, fund_code as fund_cd
, fund_desc as fund_desc
, ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(fund_amount,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float), 0) as fund_amount
, annual_giving_ind as annual_giving_ind
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as gf
where 1=1
and gift_id not in (
select gift_id
from 
<[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g
where 1=1
and gift_id not in (select gift_id from <[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g group by gift_id having count(distinct src_donor_id)>1)
and gift_id in (select gift_id from <[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g group by gift_id having count(distinct fund_code)>1)
group by gift_id having count(distinct gift_date)>1)

union all

select 
coalesce(gift_fund_id,gifts_multiple_dates_multiple_funds.calculated_field_3 || fund_code || ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(fund_amount,'[^0-9.]', '') as float), 0)) as gift_fund_id
, gifts_multiple_dates_multiple_funds.calculated_field_3 as gift_id --use gift key (bound to calculated field 3) from gifts entity for gift_id 
, fund_code as fund_cd
, fund_desc as fund_desc
, ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(fund_amount,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float), 0) as fund_amount
, annual_giving_ind as annual_giving_ind
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as gf
left join gifts_multiple_dates_multiple_funds on gifts_multiple_dates_multiple_funds.gift_id = gf.gift_id and coalesce(gifts_multiple_dates_multiple_funds.gift_date,'') = coalesce(gf.calculated_field_2,'')
where 1=1
and gf.gift_id in (
select gift_id
from 
<[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g 
where 1=1
and gift_id not in (select gift_id from <[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g group by gift_id having count(distinct src_donor_id)>1)
and gift_id in (select gift_id from <[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g group by gift_id having count(distinct fund_code)>1)
group by gift_id having count(distinct gift_date)>1
)
/*
union all

-- In case partners do not send individual records per gift allocation and instead send columns, the 2nd fund/desc/amount should be bound to calculated fields 1,2,3
select 
coalesce(gift_fund_id,gift_id || calculated_field_1) as gift_fund_id
, gift_id as gift_id
, calculated_field_1 as fund_cd
, calculated_field_2 as fund_desc
, ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(calculated_field_3,'[^0-9.]', '') as float), 0) as fund_amount
, '' as annual_giving_ind
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as gf
where 1=1

union all

-- In case partners do not send individual records per gift allocation and instead send columns, the 3rd fund/desc/amount should be bound to calculated fields 4,5,6
select 
coalesce(gift_fund_id,gift_id || calculated_field_4) as gift_fund_id
, gift_id as gift_id
, calculated_field_4 as fund_cd
, calculated_field_5 as fund_desc
, ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(calculated_field_6,'[^0-9.]', '') as float), 0) as fund_amount
, '' as annual_giving_ind
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as gf
where 1=1

union all

-- In case partners do not send individual records per gift allocation and instead send columns, the 4th fund/desc/amount should be bound to calculated fields 7,8,9
select 
coalesce(gift_fund_id,gift_id || calculated_field_7) as gift_fund_id
, gift_id as gift_id
, calculated_field_7 as fund_cd
, calculated_field_8 as fund_desc
, ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(calculated_field_9,'[^0-9.]', '') as float), 0) as fund_amount
, '' as annual_giving_ind
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as gf
where 1=1

union all

-- In case partners do not send individual records per gift allocation and instead send columns, the 5th fund/desc/amount should be bound to calculated fields 10,11,12
select 
coalesce(gift_fund_id,gift_id || calculated_field_10) as gift_fund_id
, gift_id as gift_id
, calculated_field_10 as fund_cd
, calculated_field_11 as fund_desc
, ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(calculated_field_12,'[^0-9.]', '') as float), 0) as fund_amount
, '' as annual_giving_ind

where 1=1
and fund_cd is not null -- only send records to PDP where a fund is populated. if a gift has no fund listed, it will not have any records on this final table
and ltrim(rtrim(fund_cd)) <> '' -- only send records to PDP where a fund is populated. if a gift has no fund listed, it will not have any records on this final table

--calculated_field_3 = allocation_id

with gifts_multiple_allocation_ids as (
select g.gift_id,sum(cast(regexp_replace(g.fund_amount,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float)) as total_fund_amount
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as g
where 1=1
and g.gift_id not in (select distinct gift_id from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as g where 1=1 group by gift_id having count(distinct fund_code)>1)
and coalesce(g.calculated_field_1,'') = coalesce(g.calculated_field_2,'') 
and cast(g.gift_id as varchar) is not null
and cast(g.calculated_field_1 as varchar) is not null
group by g.gift_id having count(distinct calculated_field_3)>1
) 

select 
gifts_funds.gift_fund_id
,gifts_funds.gift_id
,gifts_funds.fund_cd
,gifts_funds.fund_desc
,gifts_funds.fund_amount
,gifts_funds.annual_giving_ind
, <gifts_funds_eab_gift_is_annual_flag> as eab_gift_is_annual_flag
from 
(
select 
coalesce(gf.gift_fund_id,gf.gift_id || gf.fund_code) as gift_fund_id
, gf.gift_id as gift_id
, gf.fund_code as fund_cd
, gf.fund_desc as fund_desc
, case 
  	when gifts_multiple_allocation_ids.gift_id is not null then gifts_multiple_allocation_ids.total_fund_amount 
    else ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(gf.fund_amount,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float), 0) 
  end as fund_amount
, gf.annual_giving_ind as annual_giving_ind
,row_number() over (partition by coalesce(gf.gift_fund_id,gf.gift_id || gf.fund_code) order by 1) as rn
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as gf
left join gifts_multiple_allocation_ids on gifts_multiple_allocation_ids.gift_id = gf.gift_id
where 1=1
and coalesce(gf.calculated_field_1,'') = coalesce(gf.calculated_field_2,'')  
/*
union all

-- In case partners do not send individual records per gift allocation and instead send columns, the 2nd fund/desc/amount should be bound to calculated fields 1,2,3
select 
coalesce(gift_fund_id,gift_id || calculated_field_1) as gift_fund_id
, gift_id as gift_id
, calculated_field_1 as fund_cd
, calculated_field_2 as fund_desc
, ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(calculated_field_3,'[^0-9.]', '') as float), 0) as fund_amount
, '' as annual_giving_ind
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as gf

, '' as annual_giving_ind

, gift_id as gift_id

, ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(calculated_field_9,'[^0-9.]', '') as float), 0) as fund_amount
, '' as annual_giving_ind
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as gf
where 1=1

union all

-- In case partners do not send individual records per gift allocation and instead send columns, the 5th fund/desc/amount should be bound to calculated fields 10,11,12
select 
coalesce(gift_fund_id,gift_id || calculated_field_10) as gift_fund_id
, gift_id as gift_id
, calculated_field_10 as fund_cd
, calculated_field_11 as fund_desc
, ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(calculated_field_12,'[^0-9.]', '') as float), 0) as fund_amount
, '' as annual_giving_ind
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as gf
where 1=1
*/

where 1=1
and gifts_funds.rn=1

and ltrim(rtrim(fund_cd)) <> '' -- only send records to PDP where a fund is populated. if a gift has no fund listed, it will not have any records on this final table
				
union all
				
select 
gift_fund_id
,gift_id
,fund_cd
,fund_desc
,fund_amount
,annual_giving_ind
,eab_gift_is_annual_flag
from(
select
ga.gift_id || ga.calculated_field_2 as gift_fund_id

,ga.calculated_field_3 as fund_desc

	when calculated_field_2 in ('10000','10000-5502','MFSCHOLAR') then 'true'

end as eab_gift_is_annual_flag
, row_number() over (partition by ga.gift_id order by 1 desc) as rn

where 1=1 
and ga.gift_id not in (select distinct gift_id from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as gf 
					   where 1=1
					   and coalesce(gf.calculated_field_1,'') = coalesce(gf.calculated_field_2,'')
					  )

where 1=1
and gift_funds.rn=1
and gift_funds.fund_cd is not null -- only send records to PDP where a fund is populated. if a gift has no fund listed, it will not have any records on this final table
and ltrim(rtrim(gift_funds.fund_desc)) <> '' -- only send records to PDP where a fund is populated. if a gift has no fund listed, it will not have any records on this final table

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. queryResults.querySql:
with gifts_multiple_donor_ids as (
						  
select gift_id,sum(ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(g.gift_amount,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float), 0)) as total_gift_amount
from <[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g
where 1=1 
and gift_id not in (select distinct gift_id from <[AMS].[gifts].{fulfillment}> as g group by gift_id having count(distinct fund_code)>1)
group by gift_id having count(distinct src_donor_id)>1	
)

select 
gifts_funds.*
, <gifts_funds_eab_gift_is_annual_flag> as eab_gift_is_annual_flag
from 
(
select 
coalesce(gift_fund_id,gf.gift_id || fund_code || ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(fund_amount,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float), 0)) as gift_fund_id
, gf.gift_id as gift_id
, fund_code as fund_cd
, fund_desc as fund_desc
, case 
	 when gifts_multiple_donor_ids.gift_id is not null then gifts_multiple_donor_ids.total_gift_amount
	 else ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(fund_amount,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float), 0) 
  end as fund_amount
, annual_giving_ind as annual_giving_ind
, intake_dt
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as gf
left join gifts_multiple_donor_ids on gf.gift_id = gifts_multiple_donor_ids.gift_id													 
where 1=1

, ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(gifts_funds.fund_amount,'[^0-9.]', '') as float), 0) as fund_amount
, gifts_funds.annual_giving_ind as annual_giving_ind
, <gifts_funds_eab_gift_is_annual_flag> as eab_gift_is_annual_flag
from 
(
select 
coalesce(gift_fund_id,gift_id || fund_code) as gift_fund_id
, gift_id as gift_id
, fund_code as fund_cd
, fund_desc as fund_desc
, case 
  	when calculated_field_4 = 'Y' then ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(fund_amount,'[^0-9.]', '') as float), 0)
    else ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(calculated_field_5,'[^0-9.]', '') as float), 0)
  end as fund_amount
, annual_giving_ind as annual_giving_ind
, row_number() over (partition by coalesce(gift_fund_id,gift_id || fund_code) order by calculated_field_3 desc) as rn  
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as gf
where 1=1
and gf.calculated_field_3 = (select max(calculated_field_3) as i from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as g1 where g1.gift_id = gf.gift_id) 
and coalesce(gf.calculated_field_1,'') = coalesce(gf.calculated_field_2,'')

*/
select 
gifts_funds.gift_fund_id
,gifts_funds.gift_id
,gifts_funds.fund_cd
,gifts_funds.fund_desc
,gifts_funds.fund_amount
,gifts_funds.annual_giving_ind
, <gifts_funds_eab_gift_is_annual_flag> as eab_gift_is_annual_flag
from 
(
select 
coalesce(gf.gift_fund_id,gf.gift_id || gf.fund_code) as gift_fund_id
,gf.gift_id as gift_id
, gf.fund_code as fund_cd
, gf.fund_desc as fund_desc
, case when duplicate_gift_funds.dup_gift_fund_id is not null then duplicate_gift_funds.total_fund_amount else ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(fund_amount,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float), 0) end as fund_amount
, annual_giving_ind as annual_giving_ind
, row_number() over (partition by gf.gift_id,gf.fund_code order by 1 desc) as rn 
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as gf
left join (select 
coalesce(g.gift_fund_id,g.gift_id || g.fund_code) as dup_gift_fund_id, sum(fund_amount) as total_fund_amount
from <[AMS].[gifts_funds].{fulfillment}> as g
where 1=1
and ifnull(cast(regexp_replace(fund_amount,'[^0-9.-]', '') as float), 0)<>0
group by coalesce(g.gift_fund_id,g.gift_id || g.fund_code) having count(*)>1

select

queryResults.querySql:
/*
This bound query maps partner data to the correct
format for census student term data.  It chooses
the most recent record across all entities for
use in the individual data points.
*/

/* These CTEs are for getting these individual tables
on the correct granularity so that they can join to
par__student_term without duplicates.  This is
accomplished by assigning latest_record = 1 to the
most recent record via intake_dt */

WITH
cte_psa AS (
    SELECT
        psa.partnercontact_id
      , psa.partner_system_name
      , psa.addr1
      , psa.addr2
      , psa.city
      , psa.state AS state
      , NULL AS eab_state --no standardized field
      , psa.county
      , psa.zip AS postal_cd
      , LEFT(psa.zip, 5) AS zip5 --trimming four-digit endings
      , psa.eab_country
      , psa.country
      , psa.eab_address_type
      , psa.address_type
      , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY psa.partnercontact_id, psa.partner_system_name ORDER BY psa.intake_dt DESC) AS latest_record
    FROM <[PDP_UG].[par__student_address].{final}> psa
),

cte_pse_per AS (
    SELECT
        pse.partnercontact_id
      , pse.partner_system_name
      , pse.email AS personal_email
      , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pse.partnercontact_id, pse.partner_system_name ORDER BY pse.intake_dt DESC) AS latest_record
    FROM <[PDP_UG].[par__student_email].{final}> pse
    WHERE pse.email_type = 'Personal'
),

cte_pse_sch AS (
    SELECT
        pse.partnercontact_id
      , pse.partner_system_name
      , pse.email AS school_email
      , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pse.partnercontact_id, pse.partner_system_name ORDER BY pse.intake_dt DESC) AS latest_record
    FROM <[PDP_UG].[par__student_email].{final}> pse
    WHERE pse.email_type = 'School'
),

cte_pshs AS (
    SELECT
        pshs.partnercontact_id
      , pshs.partner_system_name
      , pshs.hs_class_rank AS class_rank
      , pshs.eab_class_rank AS eab_hs_class_rank
      , pshs.eab_hs_gpa
      , pshs.hs_gpa_nbr AS hs_gpa
      , pshs.eab_hs_gpa_type
      , pshs.hs_ceeb_cd
      , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pshs.partnercontact_id, pshs.partner_system_name ORDER BY pshs.intake_dt DESC) AS latest_record
    FROM <[PDP_UG].[par__student_high_school].{final}> pshs
),

cte_psp AS (
    SELECT
        psp.partnercontact_id
      , psp.partner_system_name
      , psp.phone_number
      , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY psp.partnercontact_id, psp.partner_system_name ORDER BY psp.intake_dt DESC) AS latest_record
    FROM <[PDP_UG].[par__student_phone].{final}> psp
),

cte_psta AS (
    SELECT
        psta.partnercontact_id
      , psta.partner_system_name
      , psta.eab_entry_term
      , psta.eab_entry_year_academic

      , psta.withdrawal_dt AS withdrawal_date

      , psta.eab_app_decision_type AS app_decision_type
      , psta.eab_app_start_ind
      , psta.eab_app_submit_ind
      , psta.eab_app_type
      , psta.app_type
      , psta.application_id
      , psta.campus_location
      , psta.eab_commuter_ind
      , psta.commuter_type
      , psta.cond_admit_reason
      , psta.full_part_time
      , psta.eab_full_part_time AS eab_full_part_time_ind
      , psta.eab_major
      , psta.major
      , psta.school_applied
      , psta.eab_test_optional_ind
      , psta.test_optional_ind
      , psta.eab_admit_ind
      , psta.admit_ind
      , psta.eab_app_complete_ind
      , psta.app_complete_ind
      , psta.eab_app_withdrawal_ind
      , psta.app_withdrawal_ind
      , psta.eab_cond_admit_ind
      , psta.cond_admit_ind
      , psta.eab_deferral_future_ind

      , psta.eab_deferral_ind

  , cte_psta.eab_deposit_ind
  , cte_psta.deposit_ind
  , cte_psta.eab_enroll_ind
  , cte_psta.enroll_ind
  , cte_psta.eab_waitlist_admit_ind
  , cte_psta.waitlist_admit_ind
  , cte_psta.eab_waitlist_ind
  , cte_psta.waitlist_ind
  , cte_psta.eab_withdrawal_ind
  , cte_psta.withdrawal_ind
  , ps.intake_dt
FROM <[PDP_UG].[par__student_term].{final}> pst
INNER JOIN <[PDP_UG].[par__student].{final}> ps
        ON pst.partnercontact_id = ps.partnercontact_id
       AND pst.partner_system_name = ps.partner_system_name
LEFT JOIN cte_psa
       ON pst.partnercontact_id = cte_psa.partnercontact_id
      AND pst.partner_system_name = cte_psa.partner_system_name
      AND cte_psa.latest_record = 1
LEFT JOIN cte_psta 
       ON pst.partnercontact_id = cte_psta.partnercontact_id
      AND pst.partner_system_name = cte_psta.partner_system_name
      AND pst.eab_entry_term = cte_psta.eab_entry_term
      AND pst.eab_entry_year_academic = cte_psta.eab_entry_year_academic
      AND pst.eab_student_type = cte_psta.eab_student_type
      AND cte_psta.latest_record = 1
LEFT JOIN cte_pshs 
       ON pst.partnercontact_id = cte_pshs.partnercontact_id
      AND pst.partner_system_name = cte_pshs.partner_system_name
      AND cte_pshs.latest_record = 1
LEFT JOIN cte_pse_per 
       ON pst.partnercontact_id = cte_pse_per.partnercontact_id
      AND pst.partner_system_name = cte_pse_per.partner_system_name
      AND cte_pse_per.latest_record = 1
LEFT JOIN cte_pse_sch 
       ON pst.partnercontact_id = cte_pse_sch.partnercontact_id
      AND pst.partner_system_name = cte_pse_sch.partner_system_name
      AND cte_pse_sch.latest_record = 1
LEFT JOIN cte_psp 
       ON pst.partnercontact_id = cte_psp.partnercontact_id
      AND pst.partner_system_name = cte_psp.partner_system_name
      AND cte_psp.latest_record = 1
LEFT JOIN cte_psyfaa 
       ON pst.partnercontact_id = cte_psyfaa.partnercontact_id
      AND pst.partner_system_name = cte_psyfaa.partner_system_name
      AND pst.eab_entry_year_academic = cte_psyfaa.eab_entry_year_academic
      AND cte_psyfaa.latest_record = 1
LEFT JOIN cte_psyfa 
       ON pst.partnercontact_id = cte_psyfa.partnercontact_id
      AND pst.partner_system_name = cte_psyfa.partner_system_name
      AND pst.eab_entry_year_academic = cte_psyfa.eab_entry_year_academic
      AND pst.eab_student_type = cte_psyfa.eab_student_type
      AND cte_psyfa.latest_record = 1
LEFT JOIN cte_psts 
       ON pst.partnercontact_id = cte_psts.partnercontact_id
      AND pst.partner_system_name = cte_psts.partner_system_name
      AND cte_psts.latest_record = 1

queryResults.sqlPreview: SELECT LPAD(attr.primary_student_id, 9, '0') AS primary_student_id , attr.entry_year_as_academic_year AS entry_year_academic , CASE WHEN attr.entry_year_as_acad…
queryResults.querySql:
SELECT
    LPAD(attr.primary_student_id, 9, '0') AS primary_student_id
  , attr.entry_year_as_academic_year AS entry_year_academic
  , CASE WHEN attr.entry_year_as_academic_year REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}$' THEN attr.entry_year_as_academic_year
           ELSE NULL
     END AS eab_entry_year_academic
  , attr.entry_term AS entry_term
  , CASE WHEN LEFT(attr.entry_term, LEN(attr.entry_term) - 5) IN ('Fall', 'Spring', 'Summer') THEN LEFT(attr.entry_term, LEN(attr.entry_term) - 5)
         ELSE 'Unknown'
    END AS eab_entry_term
  , attr.student_type AS student_type
  , DECODE(attr.student_type, 'F', 'Freshman', 'T', 'Transfer', 'R', 'Readmit', 'Unknown') AS eab_student_type

--attribute group
  , CASE WHEN attr.source_attribute_type IN ('FedFT', 'PellFT', 'StateFT', 'InstFT', 'InstMeritFT', 'InstNeedFT', 'EndowedFT', 'WaiverFT', 'AthleticFT', 'WorkFT', 'NeedLoanFT', 'NoNeedLoanFT', 'OutsideFT') THEN 'fund'
         WHEN attr.source_attribute_type IN ('ACTComposite', 'SATComposite', 'SATRComposite') THEN 'exam_score'
         WHEN attr.source_attribute_type IN ('HighSchool', 'NetDeposit', 'AWD_ACRK', 'PermanentState', 'EligMaxPell', 'EligMinPell') THEN 'custom_cohort'
         WHEN attr.source_attribute_type ILIKE 'Excl%' THEN 'excluded_group'
         ELSE 'cohort'
    END AS eab_attribute_group

--attribute type
  , attr.source_attribute_type AS src_attribute_type
  , CASE WHEN attr.source_attribute_type IN ('Asian', 'AfricanAmer', 'NativeAmer', 'White') THEN 'race'
         WHEN attr.source_attribute_type ILIKE 'Market%' THEN 'market'
         ELSE DECODE(attr.source_attribute_type,
                     'Female', 'gender',
                     'Resident', 'resident',
                     'OfColor', 'of_color',
                     'Hispanic', 'ethnicity',
                     'FMFiler', 'fm_filer',
                     'AIDAPP', 'standard_cohort', --TODO current custom mapping for fixing aidapp issue - however, more should have eab_attribute_type of 'standard_cohort'
                     'ACRK', 'academic_rank',
                     'AWD_ACRK', 'alternative_academic_rank',
                     'NDRK', 'financial_need',
                     'EFCLevel', 'financial_sai',
                     'NetDeposit', 'net_deposit',
                     'HighSchool', 'top_high_schools',
                     'ACTComposite', 'act_composite',
                     'SATComposite', 'sat_composite',
                     'SATRComposite', 'satr_composite',
                     'FedFT', 'eab_federal_fund',
                     'PellFT', 'eab_pell_fund',
                     'StateFT', 'eab_state_fund',
                     'InstFT', 'eab_institutional_fund',
                     'InstMeritFT', 'eab_institutional_merit_fund',
                     'InstNeedFT', 'eab_institutional_need_fund',
                     'EndowedFT', 'eab_endowed_fund',
                     'WaiverFT', 'eab_waiver_fund',
                     'AthleticFT', 'eab_athletic_fund',
                     'WorkFT', 'eab_work_fund',
                     'NeedLoanFT', 'eab_need_loan',
                     'NoNeedLoanFT', 'eab_no_need_loan',
                     'OutsideFT', 'eab_outside_fund',
                     'ClassRank', 'class_rank',
                     'ExclTRANSFER', 'excl_transfer',
                     'ExclPARTTIME', 'excl_parttime',
                     'ExclWAIVER', 'excl_waiver',
                     'ExclATHLETE', 'excl_athlete',
                     'ExclINTERNATIONAL', 'excl_intl',
                     'ExclINDEPENDENT', 'excl_independent',
                     'ExclNOACAD', 'excl_noacad',
                     'PermanentState', 'georgia',
                     'EligMaxPell', 'elig_max_pell',
                     'EligMinPell', 'elig_min_pell',
                     'MultiRace', 'multirace',
                     'HSGPA', 'hs_gpa',
                     'Unmapped Value'
              )
    END AS eab_attribute_type

--attribute value
  , attr.source_value
  , CASE WHEN eab_attribute_type = 'gender' THEN DECODE(attr.source_value, 0, 'Male', 1, 'Female', 2, 'Other', NULL, 'Unknown', 'Unmapped Value')
         WHEN eab_attribute_type = 'race' THEN DECODE(attr.source_attribute_type, 'Asian', 'Asian or Pacific Islander', 'AfricanAmer', 'African American', 'NativeAmer', 'American Indian or Native Alaskan', 'White', 'White', NULL, 'Unknown', 'Unmapped Value')
         WHEN eab_attribute_type IN ('academic_rank', 'alternative_academic_rank', 'financial_need', 'financial_sai', 'top_high_schools', 'act_composite', 'sat_composite', 'satr_composite', 'eab_federal_fund', 'eab_pell_fund', 'eab_state_fund', 'eab_institutional_fund', 'eab_institutional_merit_fund', 'eab_institutional_need_fund', 'eab_endowed_fund', 'eab_waiver_fund', 'eab_athletic_fund', 'eab_work_fund', 'eab_need_loan', 'eab_no_need_loan', 'eab_outside_fund', 'class_rank', 'elig_max_pell', 'elig_min_pell', 'hs_gpa') THEN attr.source_value
         WHEN eab_attribute_type IN ('resident', 'of_color', 'fm_filer', 'net_deposit', 'excl_transfer', 'excl_parttime', 'excl_waiver', 'excl_athlete', 'excl_intl', 'excl_independent', 'excl_noacad', 'multirace') THEN DECODE(attr.source_value, 1, 'TRUE', NULL)
         WHEN eab_attribute_type = 'market' THEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type)
         WHEN eab_attribute_type = 'georgia' THEN DECODE(attr.source_value, 'GA', 'TRUE', NULL)
         WHEN eab_attribute_type = 'ethnicity' THEN DECODE(attr.source_attribute_type, 'Hispanic', 'Hispanic or Latino/a/e/x', NULL)
         WHEN eab_attribute_type = 'standard_cohort' THEN 'aidapp' --TODO current custom mapping for fixing aidapp issue - however, more should have eab_attribute_type of 'standard_cohort'
         ELSE 'Unmapped Value'
    END AS eab_std_value
  , NULL AS attribute_dt
FROM <[Enroll360].[Census Student Term Attributes].{fulfillment}> AS attr
WHERE eab_std_value IS NOT NULL

queryResults.sqlPreview: --NOTE: this is JSU-Pilot specific --formatting the source data into the proper format, per ref__attribute_types' standard values SELECT LPAD(attr.primary_stude…
queryResults.querySql:
--NOTE: this is JSU-Pilot specific

--formatting the source data into the proper format, per ref__attribute_types' standard values
SELECT
    LPAD(attr.primary_student_id, 9, '0') AS primary_student_id --Uncommented because partnercontact_id and partner_system_name are sourced directly from the Enroll360 fulfillment
  , attr.partnercontact_id
  , attr.partner_system_name
  , attr.entry_year_as_academic_year AS entry_year_academic
  , CASE WHEN attr.entry_year_as_academic_year REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}$' THEN attr.entry_year_as_academic_year
           ELSE NULL
     END AS eab_entry_year_academic
  , attr.entry_term AS entry_term
  , CASE WHEN LEFT(attr.entry_term, LEN(attr.entry_term) - 5) IN ('Fall', 'Spring', 'Summer') THEN LEFT(attr.entry_term, LEN(attr.entry_term) - 5)
         ELSE 'Unknown'
    END AS eab_entry_term
  , attr.student_type AS student_type
  , DECODE(attr.student_type, 'F', 'Freshman', 'T', 'Transfer', 'R', 'Other', 'Unknown') AS eab_student_type

--attribute group
  , CASE WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) IN ('fedft', 'pellft', 'stateft', 'instft', 'instmeritft', 'instneedft', 'inststackft', 'endowedft', 'waiverft', 'athleticft', 'workft', 'noneedloanft', 'needloanft', 'outsideft') THEN 'funds'
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) = 'aid_app' THEN 'aid_app'
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) IN ('class_rank_score', 'exam_score', 'hs_gpa_score','college_gpa_score') THEN 'academic_index'
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) IN ('financial_need', 'financial_sai') THEN 'ability_to_pay'
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) = 'costtype' THEN 'fao_expense'
		 WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) = 'race' THEN 'demographic'
         ELSE 'cohort'
    END AS eab_attribute_group
  , attr.source_attribute_type AS src_attribute_type
--attribute type
  , CASE WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) IN ('fmfiler', 'resident', 'nonresident','class_rank_score', 'exam_score', 'hs_gpa_score', 'financial_need', 'financial_sai', 'race', 'college_gpa_score') THEN attr.source_attribute_type
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) = 'ofcolor' THEN 'standard_cohort'
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) = 'hispanic' THEN 'ofcolor'
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) ILIKE 'excl%' THEN 'excluded_group'
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) = 'aid_app' THEN 'aid_app'
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) = 'costtype' THEN 'expense_group'
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) IN ('fedft', 'pellft', 'stateft', 'instft', 'instmeritft', 'instneedft', 'instackft', 'endowedft', 'waiverft', 'athleticft', 'workft', 'noneedloanft', 'needloanft', 'outsideft') THEN DECODE(LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type), 'fedft', 'federal_grant', 'pellft', 'pell_grant', 'stateft', 'state_grant', 'instft', 'institutional_award', 'instmeritft', 'institutional_merit',  'instneedft', 'institutional_need', 'instackft', 'institutional_stack', 'endowedft', 'endowed_award', 'waiverft', 'tuition_waiver', 'athleticft', 'athletic_scholarship', 'workft', 'work_study', 'noneedloanft', 'no_need_loan', 'needloanft', 'need_loan', 'outsideft', 'outside_scholarship', NULL)
         ELSE 'custom_cohort'
    END AS eab_attribute_type

--attribute value
  , attr.source_value
  , CASE WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) IN ('fmfiler', 'resident', 'nonresident', 'ofcolor') THEN attr.source_attribute_type
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) = 'hispanic' THEN 'Hispanic or Latino/a/e/x'
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) ILIKE 'excl%' THEN attr.source_attribute_type
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) = 'costtype' THEN DECODE(attr.source_value, '1', 'on_campus_in_state', '2', 'off_campus_in_state', '3', 'living_with_family_in_state', '4', 'on_campus_out_of_state', '5', 'off_campus_out_of_state', '6', 'living_with_family_out_of_state', NULL)
		 WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) = 'aid_app' THEN DECODE(attr.source_value, 1, 'TRUE', 0, 'FALSE', NULL)
		 WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) IN ('eligmaxpell','pellmax') THEN 'PellMax'
		 WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) IN ('eligminpell','pellmin') THEN 'PellMin'
		 WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) IN ('pelleligible') THEN 'PellEligible'
         WHEN LOWER(attr.source_attribute_type) IN ('fedft', 'pellft', 'stateft', 'instft', 'instmeritft', 'instneedft', 'instackft', 'endowedft', 'waiverft', 'athleticft', 'workft', 'noneedloanft', 'needloanft', 'outsideft', 'race','ampnetworth','numbercollege','enrollstatus_desc','meritfromtest','entry_term','college_gpa_score') THEN attr.source_value
         ELSE attr.source_attribute_type
    END AS eab_std_value
  , TRY_CAST(attr.attribute_date AS DATE) AS attribute_dt
--select *
FROM <[Enroll360].[Census Student Term Attributes].{fulfillment}> AS attr
WHERE eab_std_value IS NOT NULL

queryRef.queryName: Enroll360.Partner Processed Census Student Term Attributes.final

queryResults.sqlPreview: /*This query source data from partner tables & deliver to <[Enroll360].[Census Student Term Attributes].[Last Validated].{final}> It chooses the most recent rec…
queryResults.querySql:
/*This query source data from partner tables & deliver to <[Enroll360].[Census Student Term Attributes].[Last Validated].{final}>
It chooses the most recent record across all entities for use in the individual data points. 

Note: All CTEs include WHERE clauses to exclude records where source_value is NULL, 
ensuring only meaningful data is getting prioritized in row_number.

JOIN Strategy: Changed all joins from LEFT JOIN to INNER JOIN in the final UNION statements 
because we only want records with populated attribute data. LEFT JOINs were creating rows 
with NULL attribute values when students had no data for specific attribute categories, 
which does not provide useful information for reporting and analysis. */


/* These CTEs are for getting these individual tables
on the correct granularity so that they can join to
par__student_term without duplicates.  This is
accomplished by assigning latest_record = 1 to the
most recent record via intake_dt */


WITH 
-- 1 Expense Group
cte_expense_group AS (
    SELECT
        pst.partnercontact_id, 
        pst.partner_system_name, 
        pst.eab_entry_year_academic, 
        pst.eab_entry_term, 
        pst.eab_student_type,
        'fao_expense' AS eab_attribute_group,
        exp.expense_group_key AS src_attribute_type, -- Maps to source attribute type identifier for expense group categorization. As per documentation, we do not have any column as expense_key. this can be a hardcoded value if required.
        'expense_group' AS eab_attribute_type,
        exp.expense_group_label AS source_value,
        exp.expense_group_key AS eab_std_value,
        exp.intake_dt AS attribute_dt,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pst.partnercontact_id, pst.partner_system_name, pst.eab_entry_year_academic, pst.eab_entry_term, pst.eab_student_type ORDER BY exp.intake_dt DESC NULLS LAST) AS latest_record
    FROM <[PDP_UG].[par__student_term].{final}> AS pst
    INNER JOIN <[PDP_UG].[par__student_year_financial_aid].{final}> AS psyfa --joining to this table to get exp_grp_key & to be able to join to exp
        ON pst.partnercontact_id     = psyfa.partnercontact_id
        AND pst.partner_system_name   = psyfa.partner_system_name
        AND pst.eab_entry_year_academic = psyfa.eab_entry_year_academic
    INNER JOIN <[PDP_UG].[par__expense_breakdown].{final}> AS exp
        ON LOWER(exp.expense_group_label) = LOWER(psyfa.eab_expense_group_key)  -- Join to bring attribute values
        AND exp.eab_entry_year_academic   = psyfa.eab_entry_year_academic      -- Added to avoid duplicates
    WHERE exp.expense_group_label IS NOT NULL
),

-- 2️ Funds
cte_funds AS (
    SELECT
        psf.partnercontact_id, 
        psf.partner_system_name, 
        psf.eab_entry_year_academic,
        'funds' AS eab_attribute_group,
        psf.EAB_COHORT_FUND_TYPE AS src_attribute_type, -- This is as per documentation. It maps to source attribute type identifier for cohort fund
        psf.EAB_FUND_TYPE AS eab_attribute_type,
        psf.eab_fund_amount AS source_value,
        psf.eab_fund_amount AS eab_std_value,
        psf.intake_dt AS attribute_dt,

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. queryResults.querySql:
WITH calculation_data AS (
    SELECT * FROM (
        SELECT DISTINCT
            nullif(trim(regexp_replace(pcr.eab_entry_year_academic,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') AS eab_entry_year_academic
          , nullif(trim(regexp_replace(pcr.eab_student_type,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') AS eab_student_type
          , nullif(trim(regexp_replace(pcr.calculation_type,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') AS calculation_type
          , nullif(trim(regexp_replace(pcr.input_value_exact,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') AS input_value_exact
          , pcr.input_value_range_min AS input_value_range_min
          , pcr.input_value_range_max AS input_value_range_max
          , CAST(pcr.calculation_output AS varchar) AS calculation_output
          , CAST(pcr.intake_date AS timestamp) AS intake_dt
        FROM <[Enroll360].[Partner Calculation Rules].{fulfillment}> AS pcr
    ) sq
    WHERE COALESCE(sq.calculation_type,'')<>''
      AND (
            COALESCE(sq.input_value_exact,'')<>''
         OR (
                sq.input_value_range_min IS NOT NULL
            AND sq.input_value_range_max IS NOT NULL
         )
      )
)

SELECT DISTINCT
    eab_entry_year_academic
  , eab_student_type
  , calculation_type
  , input_value_exact
  , input_value_range_min
  , input_value_range_max
  , calculation_output
  , intake_dt
FROM calculation_data

queryResults.querySql:
WITH calculation_data AS (
    SELECT * FROM (
        SELECT DISTINCT
            case when pdc.configuration_type = 'eab_system_type_prioritization'
				then null
				else nullif(trim(regexp_replace(pdc.eab_entry_year_academic,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') 
				end AS eab_entry_year_academic
          , case when pdc.configuration_type = 'eab_system_type_prioritization'
				then null
				else nullif(trim(regexp_replace(pdc.eab_student_type,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') 
				end AS eab_student_type
          , nullif(trim(regexp_replace(pdc.configuration_type,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') AS calculation_type
          , case when coalesce(pdc.STORED_VALUE_EXACT_OR_RANGE_MIN,'') = coalesce(pdc.STORED_VALUE_RANGE_MAX, pdc.STORED_VALUE_EXACT_OR_RANGE_MIN)
				then nullif(trim(regexp_replace(pdc.STORED_VALUE_EXACT_OR_RANGE_MIN,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') 
				else null 
				end AS input_value_exact
          , case when coalesce(pdc.STORED_VALUE_EXACT_OR_RANGE_MIN,'') = coalesce(pdc.STORED_VALUE_RANGE_MAX, pdc.STORED_VALUE_EXACT_OR_RANGE_MIN)
				then null
				else pdc.STORED_VALUE_EXACT_OR_RANGE_MIN 
				end AS input_value_range_min
          , case when coalesce(pdc.STORED_VALUE_EXACT_OR_RANGE_MIN,'') = coalesce(pdc.STORED_VALUE_RANGE_MAX, pdc.STORED_VALUE_EXACT_OR_RANGE_MIN)
				then null
				else pdc.STORED_VALUE_RANGE_MAX 
				end AS input_value_range_max
          , CAST(pdc.display_bucket_label AS varchar) AS calculation_output
          , pdc.intake_dt AS intake_dt
		FROM <[Enroll360].[Partner Display Controls].{final}> AS pdc

union all
        SELECT DISTINCT
            nullif(trim(regexp_replace(pc.eab_entry_year_academic,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') AS eab_entry_year_academic
          , nullif(trim(regexp_replace(pc.eab_student_type,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') AS eab_student_type
          , case when configuration_type = 'display_exam_type' then 'calculation_exam_type' 
				else nullif(trim(regexp_replace(pc.configuration_type,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') 
				end AS calculation_type
          , nullif(trim(regexp_replace(pc.configuration_value,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') AS input_value_exact
          , null AS input_value_range_min
          , null AS input_value_range_max
          , CAST(pc.configuration_value AS varchar) AS calculation_output
          , CAST(pc.intake_dt AS timestamp) AS intake_dt
        FROM <[Enroll360].[Partner Configurations].{final}> AS pc

    ) sq
    WHERE COALESCE(sq.calculation_type,'')<>''
      AND (COALESCE(sq.input_value_exact,'')<>''
         	OR (sq.input_value_range_min IS NOT NULL AND sq.input_value_range_max IS NOT NULL)
		  )
	  AND calculation_type in (
		'academic_index_points_band',
		'financial_need_score',
		'financial_sai_score',
		'hs_gpa_weight',
		'exam_score_weight',
		'class_rank_weight',
		'calculation_exam_type',
		'eab_system_type_prioritization',
		'merit_calc_total_academic_points_band')
)

SELECT DISTINCT
    eab_entry_year_academic
  , eab_student_type
  , calculation_type
  , input_value_exact
  , input_value_range_min
  , input_value_range_max
  , calculation_output
  , intake_dt
FROM calculation_data

order by 
    eab_entry_year_academic
  , eab_student_type
  , calculation_type
  , intake_dt
  , input_value_exact
  , input_value_range_min
  , input_value_range_max
  , calculation_output

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

reasons: Parse time improved in 5.1.4 (5.0.0-3 1098ms · 5.1.4 528ms (5.1.4 faster by 570ms))

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.
