queryResults.querySql:
WITH
latest_applications AS (
    SELECT
        app_ranked.id AS id,
        app_ranked.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
        app_ranked.updated_at AS updated_at,
        app_ranked.created_at AS created_at,
        app_ranked.primary_phone AS primary_phone,
        app_ranked.primary_phone_type AS primary_phone_type,
        app_ranked.secondary_phone AS secondary_phone,
        app_ranked.secondary_phone_type AS secondary_phone_type
    FROM (
        SELECT
            app_src.id AS id,
            app_src.prospect_id AS prospect_id,
            app_src.updated_at AS updated_at,
            app_src.created_at AS created_at,
            app_src.primary_phone AS primary_phone,
            app_src.primary_phone_type AS primary_phone_type,
            app_src.secondary_phone AS secondary_phone,
            app_src.secondary_phone_type AS secondary_phone_type,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY app_src.prospect_id
                ORDER BY
                    TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(app_src.updated_at) DESC NULLS LAST,
                    TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(app_src.created_at) DESC NULLS LAST,
                    TO_VARCHAR(app_src.id) DESC
            ) AS application_row_num
        FROM <[ECRM].[Applications].{fulfillment}> AS app_src
    ) AS app_ranked
    WHERE app_ranked.application_row_num = 1
)

SELECT
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_1,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_2,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_3,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_4,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_5,
    null as CALCULATED_ID_FIELD,
    p.intake_date as INTAKE_DATE,
    'navigate_crm_1' as PARTNER_SYSTEM_NAME,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.primary_phone)), '') AS "PHONE_NUMBER",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.primary_phone_type)), '') AS "PHONE_NUMBER_TYPE",
    NULL AS "PHONE_NUMBER_TYPE_EAB",
    null as POPULATION_NAME,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.id)), '') AS "PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID"
FROM <[ECRM].[Prospects].{fulfillment}> AS p
<student_phone_join_extension>
WHERE NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.primary_phone)), '') IS NOT NULL
  AND <student_phone_where>

UNION ALL

SELECT
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_1,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_2,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_3,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_4,
    null as CALCULATED_FIELD_5,
    null as CALCULATED_ID_FIELD,
    p.intake_date as INTAKE_DATE,
    'navigate_crm_1' as PARTNER_SYSTEM_NAME,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.secondary_phone)), '') AS "PHONE_NUMBER",
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.secondary_phone_type)), '') AS "PHONE_NUMBER_TYPE",
    NULL AS "PHONE_NUMBER_TYPE_EAB",
    null as POPULATION_NAME,
    NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(p.id)), '') AS "PRIMARY_STUDENT_ID"
FROM <[ECRM].[Prospects].{fulfillment}> AS p
LEFT JOIN latest_applications AS la
    ON la.prospect_id = p.id
<student_phone_join_extension>
WHERE NULLIF(TRIM(TO_VARCHAR(la.secondary_phone)), '') IS NOT NULL
  AND <student_phone_where>

queryResults.querySql:
/*2026-06-16: updated to align with Atlas pilot query best practices. Original version is Master: ARCHIVED_Enroll360.Student_Prior_College_PDP_Delivery.v1 
This query DOES NOT merge UG and FAO data. Row number deduping added, where variable for filtering prior to ranking and deduping - ccreekman*/

WITH 
student_prior_college_sis_fao as (
    SELECT * from (
  SELECT distinct
  	null as join_partnercontact_id, /*used for merging records only; do not delete*/
	null as join_partner_system_name, /*used for merging records only; do not delete*/
	stud_pc.*,
  row_number() over(partition by stud_pc.partnercontact_id, stud_pc.partner_system_name, stud_pc.college_ceeb_cd, lower(stud_pc.college_name)
			order by try_to_decimal(stud_pc.college_gpa_nbr, 10, 2) desc nulls last, 
				try_to_decimal(stud_pc.college_transfer_credits, 10, 2) desc nulls last, 
				stud_pc.intake_dt desc nulls last) as coll_rn

  FROM <[Enroll360].[Student Prior College SIS].[Last Validated].{final}> as stud_pc
)agg
where 1=1
and agg.coll_rn = 1
)

select * from (
select *
, row_number() over (partition by agg.partnercontact_id, agg.partner_system_name,
				    agg.college_ceeb_cd, lower(agg.college_name)
				   order by try_to_decimal(agg.college_gpa_nbr, 10, 2) desc nulls last, 
						try_to_decimal(agg.college_transfer_credits, 10, 2) desc nulls last, 
						agg.intake_dt desc nulls last) coll_rn
from (

SELECT distinct
	crm_ug.primary_student_id,

	sis_fao.eab_student_id AS eab_student_id_sis,
    sis_fao.eab_student_id_type AS eab_student_id_type_sis,
    crm_ug.eab_student_id AS eab_student_id_crm,
    crm_ug.eab_student_id_type AS eab_student_id_type_crm,
    <eab_student_id> AS eab_student_id, /*default: sis > crm*/
    <eab_student_id_type> AS eab_student_id_type, /*default: sis > crm*/

    sis_fao.partnercontact_id AS partnercontact_id_sis,
    sis_fao.partner_system_name AS partner_system_name_sis,
    crm_ug.partnercontact_id AS partnercontact_id_crm,
    crm_ug.partner_system_name AS partner_system_name_crm,
    <partnercontact_id> AS partnercontact_id, /*default: crm > join > sis*/
    <partner_system_name> AS partner_system_name, /*default: crm > join > sis*/
		
	crm_ug.college_ceeb_cd as college_ceeb_cd_crm,
	sis_fao.college_ceeb_cd as college_ceeb_cd_sis,
	<college_ceeb_cd> AS college_ceeb_cd,
	
	crm_ug.college_name as college_name_crm,
	sis_fao.college_name AS college_name_sis,
	<college_name> AS college_name,
	
	crm_ug.college_city as college_city_crm,
	sis_fao.college_city AS college_city_sis,
	<college_city> AS college_city,
	
	crm_ug.college_state as college_state_crm,
	sis_fao.college_state AS college_state_sis,
	<college_state> AS college_state,
	
	crm_ug.college_gpa_nbr as college_gpa_nbr_crm,
	sis_fao.college_gpa_nbr AS college_gpa_nbr_sis,
	<college_gpa_nbr> AS college_gpa_nbr,
	
	crm_ug.college_transfer_credits as college_transfer_credits_crm,
	sis_fao.college_transfer_credits AS college_transfer_credits_sis,
	<college_transfer_credits> AS college_transfer_credits,
	
	crm_ug.intake_dt AS intake_dt_crm,
	sis_fao.intake_dt AS intake_dt_sis,
	<intake_dt> AS intake_dt

FROM student_prior_college_sis_fao as sis_fao

<join_extension.Student Prior College PDP Delivery>

where <where_statement.Student Prior College PDP Delivery>
and (coalesce(crm_ug.partnercontact_id,'') <> '' and coalesce(crm_ug.partner_system_name,'') <> '')
or (coalesce(sis_fao.partnercontact_id,'') <> '' and coalesce(sis_fao.partner_system_name,'') <> '')

) agg

) agg2
where agg2.coll_rn = 1

queryResults.sqlPreview: /*2026-03-03: crm psname crossjoin now checks STerm to ensure we are populating pcID even if crm table does not have data, <partnercontact_id>,<partner_system_n…
queryResults.querySql:
/*2026-03-03: crm psname crossjoin now checks STerm to ensure we are populating pcID even if crm table does not have data, 
<partnercontact_id>,<partner_system_name> master bundle updated to choose ID in this order: crm ID from merged record > join ID from SIS record, SIS ID - ccreekman*/
/*2026-01-13: merge query notes - ccreekman
student_prior_college_sis_fao cte: takes all SIS data, appends any partner_system_name(s) that are present in CRM_UG Student Prior College.final
	Expectation is for one partner_system_name in CRM_UG SPC.final, but set up to account for crm changes, other scenarios where there may be a mix of ID types
	Uses this to pull in only IDs from Xwalk that align with CRM_UG SPC.final partner_system_name(s), excluding any irrelevant matching ID pairs
	if there are multiple CRM_UG SPC.final partner_system_name(s), multiple rows per SIS record will be created
	deduping logic will exclude records with null join_partnercontact_id only if there is not a record with a populated join_partnercontact_id
	multiple records per student may still persist if they have unique populated join_partnercontact_id/join_partner_system_name values
	in that scenario resulting counts on this table may be inflated, need further examples to determine if we need to build in variables to allow customization here
main query: takes results from student_prior_college_sis_fao cte and does a full outer join to CRM_UG SPC.final using the join ID / ID type (if populated)
	crm join currently in variables - unclear if we need that level of customization available
*/


WITH 
student_prior_college_sis_fao as (
    SELECT * from (
  SELECT distinct
  	id_xwalk.source_partnercontact_id as join_partnercontact_id,
	id_xwalk.source_partner_system_name as join_partner_system_name,
	stud_pc.*,
  row_number() over(partition by stud_pc.partnercontact_id, stud_pc.partner_system_name, stud_pc.college_ceeb_cd, lower(stud_pc.college_name)
		order by id_xwalk.source_partnercontact_id, try_to_decimal(stud_pc.college_gpa_nbr, 10, 2) desc nulls last, 
				try_to_decimal(stud_pc.college_transfer_credits, 10, 2) desc nulls last, 
				stud_pc.intake_dt desc nulls last) as coll_rn

  FROM <[Enroll360].[Student Prior College SIS].[Last Validated].{final}> as stud_pc

  /*cross join below will associate current crm_ug partner_system_name(s) with SIS record to limit the IDs pulled from xwalk to relevent psnames
  join parcontID/psname will later only be populated when Xwalk has records where one ID pair is the parcontID/psname from this SIS data 
  and the other set has a psname that matches what we appended here
  eg: partner xwalk includes psnames of sis_01, sis_02, primary, crm_01 but crm tables only have ID psns of primary, crm_01 so only those are appended to the records*/ 
  CROSS JOIN (
  		select distinct partner_system_name as crm_ug_partner_system_name
		FROM <[Enroll360].[Student Prior College].[Last Validated].{final}> stud_crm
		union
		select distinct partner_system_name as crm_ug_partner_system_name
		FROM <[Enroll360].[Student Term].[Last Validated].{final}> stud_crm
  		) crm_psn

  LEFT JOIN <[Enroll360].[Partner ID Xwalk].[Last Validated].{final}> id_xwalk
	on (stud_pc.partnercontact_id = id_xwalk.target_partnercontact_id
	and coalesce(stud_pc.partner_system_name,'') = coalesce(id_xwalk.target_partner_system_name,'')
	and coalesce(crm_psn.CRM_UG_PARTNER_SYSTEM_NAME,'') = coalesce(id_xwalk.source_partner_system_name,''))
)agg
where 1=1
/*xwalk may have multiple id pairs which meet join criteria
	this criteria limits the result set to only allow necessary dupes
	[coll_rn = 1]: to ensure at least one copy of the SIS record is retained regardless if there is a match in ID Xwalk
	[agg.join_partnercontact_id is not null]: any dupes with distinct partnercontact_id/partner_system_name*/

and (agg.join_partnercontact_id is not null or coll_rn = 1) 
--and agg.join_partnercontact_id is null /*for troubleshooting - SIS records with no xwalk match*/
)

select * from (
select *
, row_number() over (partition by agg.partnercontact_id, agg.partner_system_name,
				    agg.college_ceeb_cd, lower(agg.college_name)
				   order by try_to_decimal(agg.college_gpa_nbr, 10, 2) desc nulls last, 
						try_to_decimal(agg.college_transfer_credits, 10, 2) desc nulls last, 
						agg.intake_dt desc nulls last) coll_rn
from (

SELECT distinct
	crm_ug.primary_student_id,

	sis_fao.eab_student_id AS eab_student_id_sis,
    sis_fao.eab_student_id_type AS eab_student_id_type_sis,
    crm_ug.eab_student_id AS eab_student_id_crm,
    crm_ug.eab_student_id_type AS eab_student_id_type_crm,
    <eab_student_id> AS eab_student_id, /*default: sis > crm*/
    <eab_student_id_type> AS eab_student_id_type, /*default: sis > crm*/

    sis_fao.partnercontact_id AS partnercontact_id_sis,
    sis_fao.partner_system_name AS partner_system_name_sis,
    crm_ug.partnercontact_id AS partnercontact_id_crm,
    crm_ug.partner_system_name AS partner_system_name_crm,
    <partnercontact_id> AS partnercontact_id, /*default: crm > join > sis*/
    <partner_system_name> AS partner_system_name, /*default: crm > join > sis*/
		
	crm_ug.college_ceeb_cd as college_ceeb_cd_crm,
	sis_fao.college_ceeb_cd as college_ceeb_cd_sis,
	<college_ceeb_cd> AS college_ceeb_cd,
	
	crm_ug.college_name as college_name_crm,
	sis_fao.college_name AS college_name_sis,
	<college_name> AS college_name,
	
	crm_ug.college_city as college_city_crm,
	sis_fao.college_city AS college_city_sis,
	<college_city> AS college_city,
	
	crm_ug.college_state as college_state_crm,
	sis_fao.college_state AS college_state_sis,
	<college_state> AS college_state,
	
	crm_ug.college_gpa_nbr as college_gpa_nbr_crm,
	sis_fao.college_gpa_nbr AS college_gpa_nbr_sis,
	<college_gpa_nbr> AS college_gpa_nbr,
	
	crm_ug.college_transfer_credits as college_transfer_credits_crm,
	sis_fao.college_transfer_credits AS college_transfer_credits_sis,
	<college_transfer_credits> AS college_transfer_credits,
	
	crm_ug.intake_dt AS intake_dt_crm,
	sis_fao.intake_dt AS intake_dt_sis,
	<intake_dt> AS intake_dt


FROM student_prior_college_sis_fao as sis_fao

<join_extension.Student Prior College PDP Delivery>

WHERE <where_statement.Student Prior College PDP Delivery>
and (coalesce(crm_ug.partnercontact_id,'') <> '' and coalesce(crm_ug.partner_system_name,'') <> '')
or (coalesce(sis_fao.partnercontact_id,'') <> '' and coalesce(sis_fao.partner_system_name,'') <> '')

) agg

) agg2
where agg2.coll_rn = 1

order by 
	(agg2.partnercontact_id_crm||agg2.partnercontact_id_sis) nulls last, /*null in either field will return null, merged records (both fields populated) will come before non-merged records in results*/
	agg2.partnercontact_id_crm, agg2.intake_dt_crm, /*most recent non-merged UG records next*/
	agg2.partnercontact_id_sis, agg2.intake_dt_sis /*most recent non-merged FAO records next*/

queryResults.sqlPreview: /*2025-03-11: where statement is missing condition specification for SIS eab_student_id_type so defaults to evaluating for boolean and failing feed, correcting …
queryResults.querySql:
/*2025-03-11: where statement is missing condition specification for SIS eab_student_id_type so defaults to evaluating for boolean and failing feed, correcting this issue in this tenant query - ccreekman*/

WITH stud_prior_college_crm AS 
(
	SELECT
		prior_college_crm.primary_student_id AS eab_student_id_crm,
		CAST('primary' AS VARCHAR) AS eab_student_id_type_crm,
		prior_college_crm.primary_student_id,
		prior_college_crm.college_ceeb_cd AS college_ceeb_cd_crm,
		prior_college_crm.college_name AS college_name_crm,
		prior_college_crm.college_city AS college_city_crm,
		prior_college_crm.college_state AS college_state_crm,
		prior_college_crm.college_gpa_nbr AS college_gpa_nbr_crm,
		prior_college_crm.college_transfer_credits AS college_transfer_credits_crm,
		prior_college_crm.intake_dt AS intake_dt_crm
	FROM <[Enroll360].[Student Prior College].[Last Validated].{final}> as prior_college_crm
)
SELECT	
		cllg_crm.primary_student_id,
		
		cllg_sis.eab_student_id AS eab_student_id_sis,
        cllg_crm.eab_student_id_crm,
        <eab_student_id> AS eab_student_id,

		cllg_sis.eab_student_id_type AS eab_student_id_type_sis,
        cllg_crm.eab_student_id_type_crm,
        <eab_student_id_type> AS eab_student_id_type,
		
		cllg_crm.college_ceeb_cd_crm,
		cllg_sis.college_ceeb_cd AS college_ceeb_cd_sis,
		<college_ceeb_cd> AS college_ceeb_cd,
		
		cllg_crm.college_name_crm,
		cllg_sis.college_name AS college_name_sis,
		<college_name> AS college_name,
		
		cllg_crm.college_city_crm,
		cllg_sis.college_city AS college_city_sis,
		<college_city> AS college_city,
		
		cllg_crm.college_state_crm,
		cllg_sis.college_state AS college_state_sis,
		<college_state> AS college_state,
		
		cllg_crm.college_gpa_nbr_crm,
		cllg_sis.college_gpa_nbr AS college_gpa_nbr_sis,
		<college_gpa_nbr> AS college_gpa_nbr,
		
		cllg_crm.college_transfer_credits_crm,
		cllg_sis.college_transfer_credits AS college_transfer_credits_sis,
		<college_transfer_credits> AS college_transfer_credits,
		
		to_timestamp(cllg_crm.intake_dt_crm) AS intake_dt_crm,
		to_timestamp(cllg_sis.intake_dt) AS intake_dt_sis,
		to_timestamp(<intake_dt>) AS intake_dt
		
FROM <[Enroll360].[Student Prior College SIS].[Last Validated].{final}> as cllg_sis
FULL OUTER JOIN stud_prior_college_crm as cllg_crm
			ON cllg_crm.eab_student_id_crm = cllg_sis.eab_student_id
			AND cllg_crm.eab_student_id_type_crm = cllg_sis.eab_student_id_type
			AND LOWER(TRIM(COALESCE(cllg_crm.college_ceeb_cd_crm,''))) = LOWER(TRIM(COALESCE(cllg_sis.college_ceeb_cd,'')))
			AND LOWER(TRIM(COALESCE(cllg_crm.college_name_crm,''))) = LOWER(TRIM(COALESCE(cllg_sis.college_name,'')))
WHERE (cllg_sis.eab_student_id IS NOT NULL AND cllg_sis.eab_student_id_type IS NOT NULL) OR (cllg_crm.eab_student_id_crm IS NOT NULL AND cllg_crm.eab_student_id_type_crm IS NOT NULL)

queryResults.sqlPreview: /*2026-06-12: added row_number deduping at pdp key grain, priority = most recent intake date wins - ccreekman*/ /*2025-12-01: adding partner system name functio…
queryResults.querySql:
/*2026-06-12: added row_number deduping at pdp key grain, priority = most recent intake date wins - ccreekman*/
/*2025-12-01: adding partner system name functionality, variables - ccreekman*/
/*2025-07-18: added <join_extension.Student Race> - ccreekman*/
/*2025-06-19: added partnercontact_id, partner_system_name per ESANALYTIC-50473 - ccreekman*/
/*10-01-2024: eab_student_id, eab_student_id_type placeholder fields added - ccreekman*/
/*9-25-2024: per ESANALYTIC-40602, no longer returning 'Unknown' race values
if a student has no race data from any source it will be assigned Unknown downstream
reporting Unknown at this point is falsely inflating Unknown race counts in dashboards - ccreekman*/

with race_data as (
select * from (

select distinct
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(stud_race.primary_student_id,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as primary_student_id,
nullif(trim(stud_race.race),'') as race,
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(stud_race.primary_student_id,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as eab_student_id,
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(lower(regexp_replace(coalesce(stud_race.partner_system_name,'primary'),'[\\s]','')),'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as eab_student_id_type,
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(<partnercontact_id.crm_ug>,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as partnercontact_id,
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(lower(regexp_replace(<partner_system_name.crm_ug>,'[\\s]','')),'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as partner_system_name,

case when pcm_race.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race,
  
case when pcm_race_amer_indian.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_amer_indian.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_amer_indian,

case when pcm_race_asian.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_asian.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_asian,

case when pcm_race_black.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_black.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_black,

case when pcm_race_native_hawaiian.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_native_hawaiian.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_native_hawaiian,

case when pcm_race_white.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_white.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_white,

case when pcm_race_middle_eastern.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_middle_eastern.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_middle_eastern,

case when pcm_race_multiracial.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_multiracial.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_multiracial,
  
case when pcm_race_other.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_other.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_other,

case when pcm_race_prefer_not_respond.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_prefer_not_respond.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_prefer_not_respond,

/*case when pcm_race_unknown.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_unknown.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_unknown,*/
stud_race.intake_date as intake_dt

from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race
  
left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race
on (pcm_race.field_name = 'eab_race'
and coalesce(stud_race.race,'') = coalesce(pcm_race.partner_value,''))
  
left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_amer_indian
on (pcm_race_amer_indian.field_name = 'eab_race_amer_indian'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_1,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_amer_indian.partner_value,''))
  
left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_asian
on (pcm_race_asian.field_name = 'eab_race_asian'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_2,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_asian.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_black
on (pcm_race_black.field_name = 'eab_race_black'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_3,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_black.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_native_hawaiian
on (pcm_race_native_hawaiian.field_name = 'eab_race_native_hawaiian'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_4,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_native_hawaiian.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_white
on (pcm_race_white.field_name = 'eab_race_white'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_5,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_white.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_middle_eastern
on (pcm_race_middle_eastern.field_name = 'eab_race_middle_eastern'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_6,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_middle_eastern.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_multiracial
on (pcm_race_multiracial.field_name = 'eab_race_multiracial'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_7,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_multiracial.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_other
on (pcm_race_other.field_name = 'eab_race_other'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_8,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_other.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_prefer_not_respond
on (pcm_race_prefer_not_respond.field_name = 'eab_race_prefer_not_respond'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_9,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_prefer_not_respond.partner_value,''))

/*left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_unknown
on (pcm_race_unknown.field_name = 'eab_race_unknown'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_10,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_unknown.partner_value,''))*/

<join_extension.Student Race>
												  
where 1=1									  

) agg

where coalesce(agg.partnercontact_id,'') <> ''
)




select
agg2.primary_student_id,
agg2.race,
agg2.eab_race,
agg2.eab_student_id,
agg2.eab_student_id_type,
agg2.partnercontact_id,
agg2.partner_system_name,
agg2.intake_dt

from (
select agg.*,
row_number() over(partition by agg.partnercontact_id, agg.partner_system_name, agg.eab_race
				  order by agg.intake_dt desc nulls last) as race_rn
  
from (	
select primary_student_id
, race
, case 
	when eab_race in ('Asian/Asian American','Asian') then 'Asian'
	else eab_race
	end as eab_race
, eab_student_id
, eab_student_id_type
, partnercontact_id
, partner_system_name
, intake_dt	
from race_data
--where eab_race is not null and race <> ''
where coalesce(eab_race,'') not in ('Unknown','Unmapped Value','') and race <> ''

	
union all

select primary_student_id
, EAB_RACE_AMER_INDIAN
, EAB_RACE_AMER_INDIAN
, eab_student_id
, eab_student_id_type
, partnercontact_id
, partner_system_name
, intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_AMER_INDIAN is not null
	
union all

select primary_student_id
, EAB_RACE_ASIAN
, case 
	when EAB_RACE_ASIAN in ('Asian/Asian American','Asian') then 'Asian'
	else null
	end as EAB_RACE_ASIAN
, eab_student_id
, eab_student_id_type
, partnercontact_id
, partner_system_name
, intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_ASIAN is not null
	
union all

select primary_student_id
, EAB_RACE_BLACK
, EAB_RACE_BLACK
, eab_student_id
, eab_student_id_type
, partnercontact_id
, partner_system_name
, intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_BLACK is not null

union all

select primary_student_id
, EAB_RACE_NATIVE_HAWAIIAN
, EAB_RACE_NATIVE_HAWAIIAN
, eab_student_id
, eab_student_id_type
, partnercontact_id
, partner_system_name
, intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_NATIVE_HAWAIIAN is not null

union all

select primary_student_id
, EAB_RACE_WHITE
, EAB_RACE_WHITE
, eab_student_id
, eab_student_id_type
, partnercontact_id
, partner_system_name
, intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_WHITE is not null

union all

select primary_student_id
, EAB_RACE_MIDDLE_EASTERN
, EAB_RACE_MIDDLE_EASTERN
, eab_student_id
, eab_student_id_type
, partnercontact_id
, partner_system_name
, intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_MIDDLE_EASTERN is not null

union all

select primary_student_id
, EAB_RACE_MULTIRACIAL
, EAB_RACE_MULTIRACIAL
, eab_student_id
, eab_student_id_type
, partnercontact_id
, partner_system_name
, intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_MULTIRACIAL is not null

union all

select primary_student_id
, EAB_RACE_OTHER
, EAB_RACE_OTHER
, eab_student_id
, eab_student_id_type
, partnercontact_id
, partner_system_name
, intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_OTHER is not null

union all

select primary_student_id
, EAB_RACE_PREFER_NOT_RESPOND
, EAB_RACE_PREFER_NOT_RESPOND
, eab_student_id
, eab_student_id_type
, partnercontact_id
, partner_system_name
, intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_PREFER_NOT_RESPOND is not null

/*union all

select primary_student_id
, EAB_RACE_UNKNOWN
, EAB_RACE_UNKNOWN
, eab_student_id
, eab_student_id_type
, partnercontact_id
, partner_system_name
, intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_UNKNOWN is not null*/
  
) agg
where coalesce(agg.partnercontact_id,'') <> ''
and coalesce(agg.partner_system_name,'') <> ''

) agg2
where agg2.race_rn = 1

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

queryResults.querySql:
/*6-20-2023: Franklin Pierce has an unusual race set up. Race is only in ug_apps. Race is divided between 4 fields. Fields are not specific to single race.
therefore we must look across all 4 fields to identify the student's race. - ccreekman, bpevarski*/


select distinct 
agg.primary_student_id,
agg.race_rollup as race,
agg.eab_race

from (
select 
stud_race.primary_student_id as primary_student_id,
case when stud_race.calculated_field_1 like '%American Indian%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_2 like '%American Indian%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_3 like '%American Indian%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_4 like '%American Indian%'
	then 'American Indian' else null end as race_rollup,
'American Indian/Alaska Native' as eab_race
from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race
where race_rollup is not null
 
union all

select
stud_race.primary_student_id as primary_student_id,
case when stud_race.calculated_field_1 like '%Asian%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_2 like '%Asian%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_3 like '%Asian%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_4 like '%Asian%'
	then 'Asian' else null end as race_rollup,
'Asian' as eab_race
from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race
where race_rollup is not null
union all

select
stud_race.primary_student_id as primary_student_id,
case when stud_race.calculated_field_1 like '%Black%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_2 like '%Black%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_3 like '%Black%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_4 like '%Black%'
	then 'Black' else null end as race_rollup,
'Black/African American' as eab_race
from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race
where race_rollup is not null
union all

select
stud_race.primary_student_id as primary_student_id,
case when stud_race.calculated_field_1 like '%Native Hawaiian%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_2 like '%Native Hawaiian%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_3 like '%Native Hawaiian%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_4 like '%Native Hawaiian%'
	then 'Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander' else null end as race_rollup,
'Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander' as eab_race
from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race
where race_rollup is not null
union all

select
stud_race.primary_student_id as primary_student_id,
case when stud_race.calculated_field_1 like '%White%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_2 like '%White%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_3 like '%White%'
	or stud_race.calculated_field_4 like '%White%'
	then 'White' else null end as race_rollup,
'White' as eab_race
from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race
where race_rollup is not null
union all

select
stud_race.primary_student_id as primary_student_id,
case when coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_1,'') = '' 
	and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_2,'') = '' 
	and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_3,'') = '' 
	and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_4,'') = '' 
	then 'Unknown' else null end as race_rollup,
'Unknown' as eab_race 
from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race
where race_rollup is not null
) agg

where agg.primary_student_id is not null

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

/*2025-08-07: solved in bindings by concatenating fields and treating like delimited race field, creating blank ug_inqs fulfillment and moving to multifile master - ccreekman*/

therefore we must look across all 4 fields to identify the student's race. - ccreekman, bpevarski*/

select distinct * from (
select distinct 
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(agg.primary_student_id,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as primary_student_id,
nullif(trim(agg.race_rollup),'') as race,
case when race_rollup = 'Unknown'
then 'Unknown'
when pcm_race.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race,

nullif(trim(regexp_replace(agg.eab_student_id,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as eab_student_id,
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(agg.eab_student_id_type,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as eab_student_id_type,
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(agg.eab_student_id,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as partnercontact_id,
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(agg.eab_student_id_type,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as partner_system_name,
agg.intake_dt

from (
select 
stud_race.primary_student_id as primary_student_id,
case when stud_race.calculated_field_1 like '%American Indian%'
	then stud_race.calculated_field_1
	when stud_race.calculated_field_2 like '%American Indian%'
	then stud_race.calculated_field_2
	when stud_race.calculated_field_3 like '%American Indian%'
	then stud_race.calculated_field_3
	when stud_race.calculated_field_4 like '%American Indian%'
	then stud_race.calculated_field_4
	else null end as race_rollup,

stud_race.primary_student_id as eab_student_id,
'primary' as eab_student_id_type,
stud_race.intake_date as intake_dt

from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race
 
where race_rollup is not null
 
union all

select
stud_race.primary_student_id as primary_student_id,

	then stud_race.calculated_field_4

from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race

union all

	then stud_race.calculated_field_2

	then stud_race.calculated_field_3

	then stud_race.calculated_field_4
	else null end as race_rollup,
stud_race.primary_student_id as eab_student_id,
'primary' as eab_student_id_type,
stud_race.intake_date as intake_dt

from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race
where race_rollup is not null
union all

select
stud_race.primary_student_id as primary_student_id,
case when stud_race.calculated_field_1 like '%White%'
	then stud_race.calculated_field_1
	when stud_race.calculated_field_2 like '%White%'
	then stud_race.calculated_field_2
	when stud_race.calculated_field_3 like '%White%'
	then stud_race.calculated_field_3
	when stud_race.calculated_field_4 like '%White%'
	then stud_race.calculated_field_4
	else null end as race_rollup,
stud_race.primary_student_id as eab_student_id,
'primary' as eab_student_id_type,
stud_race.intake_date as intake_dt

from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race
where race_rollup is not null
union all

select
stud_race.primary_student_id as primary_student_id,
case when coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_1,'') = '' 
	and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_2,'') = '' 
	and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_3,'') = '' 
	and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_4,'') = '' 
	then 'Unknown' else null end as race_rollup,
stud_race.primary_student_id as eab_student_id,
null as eab_student_id_type,
stud_race.intake_date as intake_dt

from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race
where race_rollup is not null
) agg

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race
on (pcm_race.field_name = 'eab_race'
and coalesce(agg.race_rollup,'') = coalesce(pcm_race.partner_value,''))

where  1=1
and coalesce(eab_race,'') not in ('Unknown','Unmapped Value','')

) agg2
where coalesce(agg2.partnercontact_id,'') <> ''
and coalesce(agg2.partner_system_name,'') <> ''

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

/*2025-11-04: testing partner system name functionality, variables - ccreekman*/
/*2025-07-18: added <join_extension.Student Race> - ccreekman*/
/*2025-06-19: added partnercontact_id, partner_system_name per ESANALYTIC-50473 - ccreekman*/
/*10-01-2024: eab_student_id, eab_student_id_type placeholder fields added - ccreekman*/
/*9-25-2024: per ESANALYTIC-40602, no longer returning 'Unknown' race values
if a student has no race data from any source it will be assigned Unknown downstream
reporting Unknown at this point is falsely inflating Unknown race counts in dashboards - ccreekman*/

with race_data as (
select * from (

select distinct
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(stud_race.primary_student_id,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as primary_student_id,
nullif(trim(stud_race.race),'') as race,
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(stud_race.primary_student_id,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as eab_student_id,
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(lower(regexp_replace(coalesce(stud_race.partner_system_name,'primary'),'[\\s]','')),'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as eab_student_id_type,
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(<partnercontact_id.crm_ug>,'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as partnercontact_id,
nullif(trim(regexp_replace(lower(regexp_replace(<partner_system_name.crm_ug>,'[\\s]','')),'"|[\\000-\\037\\177]','')),'') as partner_system_name,

case when pcm_race.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race,
  
case when pcm_race_amer_indian.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_amer_indian.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_amer_indian,

case when pcm_race_asian.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_asian.eab_standard_value

else pcm_race_multiracial.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_multiracial,
  
case when pcm_race_other.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_other.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_other,

then null
else pcm_race_prefer_not_respond.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_prefer_not_respond,

then null
else pcm_race_unknown.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_unknown,*/
stud_race.intake_date as intake_dt

from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race
  
left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race
on (pcm_race.field_name = 'eab_race'

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_native_hawaiian

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_multiracial

and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_7,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_multiracial.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_other
on (pcm_race_other.field_name = 'eab_race_other'

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_prefer_not_respond

and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_9,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_prefer_not_respond.partner_value,''))

and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_10,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_unknown.partner_value,''))*/

<join_extension.Student Race>
												  
where 1=1

where coalesce(agg.partnercontact_id,'') <> ''
)

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

nullif(trim(stud_race.race),'') as race,
  
case when pcm_race.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then 'Unknown'
else pcm_race.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race,
  
case when pcm_race_amer_indian.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_amer_indian.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_amer_indian,

case when pcm_race_asian.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_asian.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_asian,

case when pcm_race_black.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_black.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_black,

case when pcm_race_native_hawaiian.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_native_hawaiian.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_native_hawaiian,

case when pcm_race_white.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_white.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_white,

case when pcm_race_middle_eastern.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_middle_eastern.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_middle_eastern,

case when pcm_race_multiracial.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_multiracial.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_multiracial,
  
case when pcm_race_other.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_other.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_other,

case when pcm_race_prefer_not_respond.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_prefer_not_respond.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_prefer_not_respond,

case when pcm_race_unknown.eab_standard_value = 'Unmapped Value'
then null
else pcm_race_unknown.eab_standard_value
end as eab_race_unknown,
stud_race.intake_date as intake_dt

from <[Enroll360].[Student Race].{fulfillment}> as stud_race

join <[Enroll360].[Student Term].{fulfillment}> st
on stud_race.primary_student_id = st.primary_student_id
and st.student_type = 'High school student or traditional transfer'

join <[Enroll360].[Student Relationship].{ProgramTerm}> pt
	on st.current_entry_term = pt.calculated_field_10
  	and pt.calculated_field_10 != 'Unknown'
  	and substring(pt.calculated_field_11,1,4) >= substring(sysdate(),1,4)

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race

and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_1,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_amer_indian.partner_value,''))
  
left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_asian

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_black

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_native_hawaiian

and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_4,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_native_hawaiian.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_white
on (pcm_race_white.field_name = 'eab_race_white'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_5,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_white.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_middle_eastern
on (pcm_race_middle_eastern.field_name = 'eab_race_middle_eastern'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_6,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_middle_eastern.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_multiracial
on (pcm_race_multiracial.field_name = 'eab_race_multiracial'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_7,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_multiracial.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_other
on (pcm_race_other.field_name = 'eab_race_other'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_8,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_other.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_prefer_not_respond
on (pcm_race_prefer_not_respond.field_name = 'eab_race_prefer_not_respond'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_9,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_prefer_not_respond.partner_value,''))

left outer join <[Enroll360].[Partner Code Mapping].{convert}> pcm_race_unknown
on (pcm_race_unknown.field_name = 'eab_race_unknown'
and coalesce(stud_race.calculated_field_10,'') = coalesce(pcm_race_unknown.partner_value,''))
														  
where <where_statement>											  
and coalesce(stud_race.primary_student_id,'') <> '')

from race_data

union all

,intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_MIDDLE_EASTERN is not null

union all

select primary_student_id

,intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_MULTIRACIAL is not null

union all

select primary_student_id
, EAB_RACE_OTHER
, EAB_RACE_OTHER
,intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_OTHER is not null

union all

select primary_student_id
, EAB_RACE_PREFER_NOT_RESPOND
, EAB_RACE_PREFER_NOT_RESPOND
,intake_dt
from race_data
where EAB_RACE_PREFER_NOT_RESPOND is not null

union all

select primary_student_id

,intake_dt

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

setOpInterfaceDistinctness.authorGuidance: PSS 5.1.4 builds a per-branch output interface from select-list output names. Each UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT branch must expose the same number of distinct interface columns with pairwise-compatible types. Repeating the same unaliased column reference (for example `t.col` twice) produces duplicate interface names; the parser deduplicates them to one key, which can trigger SET_OPERATION_INTERFACE_COLUMN_COUNT_MISMATCH even when the raw SELECT list looks wider. Fix: add a unique `AS alias` on every select item in every set-op branch so each output column has a distinct interface name. When the author asks for help, propose concrete aliases for every duplicate occurrence after the first.

queryResults.querySql:
/*2026-06-23: updated to align with Atlas pilot query best practices. This query DOES NOT merge UG and FAO data.  - ccreekman*/
/*2026-06-23: added where statement variable for filtering prior to ranking and deduping - ccreekman*/

WITH 
student_race_sis_fao as (
    SELECT * from (
  SELECT distinct
  	null as join_partnercontact_id, /*used for merging records only; do not delete*/
	null as join_partner_system_name, /*used for merging records only; do not delete*/
	stud_race.*,
  row_number() over(partition by stud_race.partnercontact_id, stud_race.partner_system_name, lower(stud_race.eab_race)
		order by intake_dt desc nulls last) as race_rn

  FROM <[Enroll360].[Student Race SIS].[Last Validated].{final}> as stud_race

) agg
where 1=1
and race_rn = 1 

)

select * from (
select *
, row_number() over (partition by agg.partnercontact_id, agg.partner_system_name, lower(agg.eab_race)
				   order by agg.intake_dt desc nulls last) pdp_delivery_rn
from (
SELECT
	crm_ug.primary_student_id,

	sis_fao.eab_student_id AS eab_student_id_sis,
    sis_fao.eab_student_id_type AS eab_student_id_type_sis,
    crm_ug.eab_student_id AS eab_student_id_crm,
    crm_ug.eab_student_id_type AS eab_student_id_type_crm,
    <eab_student_id> AS eab_student_id, /*default: sis > crm*/
    <eab_student_id_type> AS eab_student_id_type, /*default: sis > crm*/

    sis_fao.partnercontact_id AS partnercontact_id_sis,
    sis_fao.partner_system_name AS partner_system_name_sis,
    crm_ug.partnercontact_id AS partnercontact_id_crm,
    crm_ug.partner_system_name AS partner_system_name_crm,
    <partnercontact_id> AS partnercontact_id, /*default: crm > join > sis*/
    <partner_system_name> AS partner_system_name, /*default: crm > join > sis*/

		crm_ug.race AS race_crm,
		sis_fao.race AS race_sis,
		<race> AS race,
		
		crm_ug.eab_race as eab_race_crm,
		sis_fao.eab_race AS eab_race_sis,
		<eab_race> AS eab_race,
		
		to_timestamp(crm_ug.intake_dt) AS intake_dt_crm,
		to_timestamp(sis_fao.intake_dt) AS intake_dt_sis,
		to_timestamp(<intake_dt>) AS intake_dt
		
FROM student_race_sis_fao as sis_fao

<join_extension.Student Race PDP Delivery>

WHERE <where_statement.Student Race PDP Delivery>
and (coalesce(crm_ug.partnercontact_id,'') <> '' and coalesce(crm_ug.partner_system_name,'') <> '')
or (coalesce(sis_fao.partnercontact_id,'') <> '' and coalesce(sis_fao.partner_system_name,'') <> '')

) agg

) agg2
where agg2.pdp_delivery_rn = 1



/***********************************************************/

/**2026-06-23: prev version below**/
/*2026-03-03: <partnercontact_id>,<partner_system_name> master bundle updated to choose ID in this order: crm ID from merged record > join ID from SIS record, SIS ID 
join fields are in merge query, null placeholder fields added to this query 
ID fields were not in alignment with rest of PDP Delivery masters - corrected - ccreekman*/

		stu_race.partnercontact_id as partnercontact_id_crm,
  		stu_race.partner_system_name as partner_system_name_crm,
		stu_race.race AS race_crm,
		stu_race.eab_race AS eab_race_crm,
		stu_race.intake_dt AS intake_dt_crm,
  		stu_race.primary_student_id AS primary_student_id_crm,
		null as join_partnercontact_id,
		null as join_partner_system_name

	FROM <[Enroll360].[Student Race].[Last Validated].{final}> as stu_race
) 
SELECT
	stu_race_crm.primary_student_id,

	stu_race_crm.eab_student_id_crm,
    stud_race_sis.eab_student_id AS eab_student_id_sis,
    <eab_student_id> AS eab_student_id, --default: sis > crm

    stu_race_crm.eab_student_id_type_crm,
	stud_race_sis.eab_student_id_type AS eab_student_id_type_sis,
    <eab_student_id_type> AS eab_student_id_type, --default: sis > crm
	
	stu_race_crm.partnercontact_id_crm,
    stud_race_sis.partnercontact_id AS partnercontact_id_sis,
	<partnercontact_id> AS partnercontact_id, --default: crm > join > sis
	
	stu_race_crm.partner_system_name_crm,
    stud_race_sis.partner_system_name AS partner_system_name_sis, 
	<partner_system_name> AS partner_system_name, --default: crm > join > sis
	
		stu_race_crm.race_crm,
		stud_race_sis.race AS race_sis,
		<race> AS race,
		
		stu_race_crm.eab_race_crm,
		stud_race_sis.eab_race AS eab_race_sis,
		<eab_race> AS eab_race,

FROM <[Enroll360].[Student Race SIS].[Last Validated].{final}> as stud_race_sis
FULL OUTER JOIN race_crm as stu_race_crm
			ON 	stu_race_crm.eab_student_id_crm = stud_race_sis.eab_student_id
			AND stu_race_crm.eab_student_id_type_crm = stud_race_sis.eab_student_id_type

WHERE (stud_race_sis.eab_student_id IS NOT NULL AND stud_race_sis.eab_student_id_type IS NOT NULL) OR (stu_race_crm.eab_student_id_crm IS NOT NULL AND stu_race_crm.eab_student_id_type_crm IS NOT NULL)

*/

	SELECT

	FROM <[Enroll360].[Student Race].[Last Validated].{final}> as stu_race

SELECT
		stu_race_crm.primary_student_id_crm AS primary_student_id,
		stud_race_sis.eab_student_id AS eab_student_id_sis,
        stu_race_crm.eab_student_id_crm,
        <eab_student_id> AS eab_student_id,

		stud_race_sis.eab_student_id_type AS eab_student_id_type_sis,
        stu_race_crm.eab_student_id_type_crm,
        <eab_student_id_type> AS eab_student_id_type,

		stu_race_crm.race_crm,
		stud_race_sis.race AS race_sis,
		<race> AS race,
		
		stu_race_crm.eab_race_crm,
		stud_race_sis.eab_race AS eab_race_sis,
		<eab_race> AS eab_race,
		
		to_timestamp(stu_race_crm.intake_dt_crm) AS intake_dt_crm,
		to_timestamp(stud_race_sis.intake_dt) AS intake_dt_sis,
		to_timestamp(<intake_dt>) AS intake_dt

FULL OUTER JOIN race_crm as stu_race_crm
			ON 	stu_race_crm.eab_student_id_crm = stud_race_sis.eab_student_id
			AND stu_race_crm.eab_student_id_type_crm = stud_race_sis.eab_student_id_type
			AND LOWER(stu_race_crm.eab_race_crm) = LOWER(stud_race_sis.eab_race)

queryResults.querySql:
/*2026-06-23: added where statement variable for filtering prior to ranking and deduping - ccreekman*/
/*2026-03-03: crm psname crossjoin now checks STerm to ensure we are populating pcID even if crm table does not have data, 
<partnercontact_id>,<partner_system_name> master bundle updated to choose ID in this order: crm ID from merged record > join ID from SIS record, SIS ID - ccreekman*/
/*2026-02-06: merge query notes - ccreekman
student_race_sis_fao cte: takes all SIS data, appends any partner_system_name(s) that are present in CRM_UG Student Race.final
	Expectation is for one partner_system_name in CRM_UG Student Race.final, but set up to account for crm changes, other scenarios where there may be a mix of ID types
	Uses this to pull in only IDs from Xwalk that align with CRM_UG Student Race.final partner_system_name(s), excluding any irrelevant matching ID pairs
	if there are multiple CRM_UG Student Race.final partner_system_name(s), multiple rows per SIS record will be created
	deduping logic will exclude records with null join_partnercontact_id only if there is not a record with a populated join_partnercontact_id
	multiple records per student may still persist if they have unique populated join_partnercontact_id/join_partner_system_name values
	in that scenario resulting counts on this table may be inflated, need further examples to determine if we need to build in variables to allow customization here
main query: takes results from student_race_sis_fao cte and does a full outer join to CRM_UG Student Race.final using the join ID / ID type / eab_race (if populated)
	crm join currently in variables - unclear if we need that level of customization available
*/

WITH 
student_race_sis_fao as (
    SELECT * from (
  SELECT distinct
  	id_xwalk.source_partnercontact_id as join_partnercontact_id,
	id_xwalk.source_partner_system_name as join_partner_system_name,
	stud_race.*,
  row_number() over(partition by stud_race.partnercontact_id, stud_race.partner_system_name, lower(stud_race.eab_race)
		order by id_xwalk.source_partnercontact_id) as rn

  FROM <[Enroll360].[Student Race SIS].[Last Validated].{final}> as stud_race

  /*cross join below will associate current crm_ug partner_system_name(s) with SIS record to limit the IDs pulled from xwalk to relevent psnames
  join parcontID/psname will later only be populated when Xwalk has records where one ID pair is the parcontID/psname from this SIS data 
  and the other set has a psname that matches what we appended here
  eg: partner xwalk includes psnames of sis_01, sis_02, primary, crm_01 but crm tables only have ID psns of primary, crm_01 so only those are appended to the records*/ 
  CROSS JOIN (
  		select distinct partner_system_name as crm_ug_partner_system_name
		FROM <[Enroll360].[Student Race].[Last Validated].{final}> stud_addr_crm
		union
		select distinct partner_system_name as crm_ug_partner_system_name
		FROM <[Enroll360].[Student Term].[Last Validated].{final}> stud_addr_crm
  		) crm_psn

  LEFT JOIN <[Enroll360].[Partner ID Xwalk].[Last Validated].{final}> id_xwalk
	on (stud_race.partnercontact_id = id_xwalk.target_partnercontact_id
	and coalesce(stud_race.partner_system_name,'') = coalesce(id_xwalk.target_partner_system_name,'')
	and coalesce(crm_psn.CRM_UG_PARTNER_SYSTEM_NAME,'') = coalesce(id_xwalk.source_partner_system_name,''))
)agg
where 1=1
/*xwalk may have multiple id pairs which meet join criteria
	this criteria limits the result set to only allow necessary dupes
	[rn = 1]: to ensure at least one copy of the SIS record is retained regardless if there is a match in ID Xwalk
	[agg.join_partnercontact_id is not null]: any dupes with distinct partnercontact_id/partner_system_name*/

and (agg.join_partnercontact_id is not null or rn = 1) 
--and agg.join_partnercontact_id is null /*for troubleshooting - SIS records with no xwalk match*/
)

select * from (
select *
, row_number() over (partition by agg.partnercontact_id, agg.partner_system_name, lower(agg.eab_race)
				   order by agg.intake_dt desc nulls last) pdp_delivery_rn
from (
SELECT
	crm_ug.primary_student_id,

	sis_fao.eab_student_id AS eab_student_id_sis,
    sis_fao.eab_student_id_type AS eab_student_id_type_sis,
    crm_ug.eab_student_id AS eab_student_id_crm,
    crm_ug.eab_student_id_type AS eab_student_id_type_crm,
    <eab_student_id> AS eab_student_id, /*default: sis > crm*/
    <eab_student_id_type> AS eab_student_id_type, /*default: sis > crm*/

    sis_fao.partnercontact_id AS partnercontact_id_sis,
    sis_fao.partner_system_name AS partner_system_name_sis,
    crm_ug.partnercontact_id AS partnercontact_id_crm,
    crm_ug.partner_system_name AS partner_system_name_crm,
    <partnercontact_id> AS partnercontact_id, /*default: crm > join > sis*/
    <partner_system_name> AS partner_system_name, /*default: crm > join > sis*/

		crm_ug.race AS race_crm,
		sis_fao.race AS race_sis,
		<race> AS race,
		
		crm_ug.eab_race as eab_race_crm,
		sis_fao.eab_race AS eab_race_sis,
		<eab_race> AS eab_race,
		
		to_timestamp(crm_ug.intake_dt) AS intake_dt_crm,
		to_timestamp(sis_fao.intake_dt) AS intake_dt_sis,
		to_timestamp(<intake_dt>) AS intake_dt
		
FROM student_race_sis_fao as sis_fao

<join_extension.Student Race PDP Delivery>

WHERE <where_statement.Student Race PDP Delivery>
and (coalesce(crm_ug.partnercontact_id,'') <> '' and coalesce(crm_ug.partner_system_name,'') <> '')
or (coalesce(sis_fao.partnercontact_id,'') <> '' and coalesce(sis_fao.partner_system_name,'') <> '')

) agg

) agg2
where agg2.pdp_delivery_rn = 1

order by 
	(agg2.partnercontact_id_crm||agg2.partnercontact_id_sis) nulls last, /*null in either field will return null, merged records (both fields populated) will come before non-merged records in results*/
	agg2.partnercontact_id_crm, agg2.intake_dt_crm, /*most recent non-merged UG records next*/
	agg2.partnercontact_id_sis, agg2.intake_dt_sis /*most recent non-merged FAO records next*/
